verses.text: Abram said to Lot, “Please, let there be no strife between you and me, and between your herdsmen and my herdsmen; for we are relatives.”
verses.meaning: Abram chose family over winning. When conflict grows, you can be the first one to ask for peace.
verses.kjv: And Abram said unto Lot, Let there be no strife, I pray thee, between me and thee, and between my herdmen and thy herdmen; for we be brethren.

verses.text: Then he said to them, “Go your way. Eat the fat, drink the sweet, and send portions to him for whom nothing is prepared, for today is holy to our Lord. Don’t be grieved, for the joy of the LORD is your strength.”
verses.meaning: Grief over your failures isn’t the end. Delight in God, share with others, and let that joy hold you up.
verses.kjv: Then he said unto them, Go your way, eat the fat, and drink the sweet, and send portions unto them for whom nothing is prepared: for this day is holy unto our Lord: neither be ye sorry; for the joy of the LORD is your strength.

verses.text: You count my wanderings. You put my tears into your container. Aren’t they in your book?
verses.meaning: God keeps track of every restless night and every tear. None of your pain slips past him.
verses.kjv: Thou tellest my wanderings: put thou my tears into thy bottle: are they not in thy book?

verses.text: Praise the LORD, my soul, and don’t forget all his benefits…
verses.meaning: Gratitude fades when memory does. Talk to your own soul and list what God has already done for you.
verses.kjv: Bless the LORD, O my soul, and forget not all his benefits…

verses.text: Jacob served seven years for Rachel. They seemed to him but a few days, for the love he had for her.
verses.meaning: Jacob’s seven years of work for Rachel flew by. When you truly love someone, sacrifice feels light.
verses.kjv: And Jacob served seven years for Rachel; and they seemed unto him but a few days, for the love he had to her.

verses.text: The LORD God took the man, and put him into the garden of Eden to cultivate and keep it.
verses.meaning: Before anything went wrong, God gave people work: tending his world. Work is part of the good design.
verses.kjv: And the LORD God took the man, and put him into the garden of Eden to dress it and to keep it.

verses.text: Now let a little water be fetched, wash your feet, and rest yourselves under the tree.
verses.meaning: Abraham welcomed tired strangers with water for their feet and a shady tree. Offering rest is a gift.
verses.kjv: Let a little water, I pray you, be fetched, and wash your feet, and rest yourselves under the tree…

verses.text: I wait for the LORD. My soul waits. I hope in his word.
verses.meaning: Waiting is hard, but it doesn’t have to be empty. You can wait on God, hoping in what he’s promised.
verses.kjv: I wait for the LORD, my soul doth wait, and in his word do I hope.

verses.text: Now don’t be grieved, nor angry with yourselves, that you sold me here, for God sent me before you to preserve life.
verses.meaning: Joseph met the brothers who sold him with grace, not revenge, and told them to stop punishing themselves.
verses.kjv: Now therefore be not grieved, nor angry with yourselves, that ye sold me hither: for God did send me before you to preserve life.

verses.text: He said, “Certainly I will be with you. This will be the token to you, that I have sent you: when you have brought the people out of Egypt, you shall serve God on this mountain.”
verses.meaning: Moses felt unqualified. God didn’t list his strengths; he simply promised to go with him. That was enough.
verses.kjv: And he said, Certainly I will be with thee; and this shall be a token unto thee, that I have sent thee: When thou hast brought forth the people out of Egypt, ye shall serve God upon this mountain.

verses.text: If you do well, won’t it be lifted up? If you don’t do well, sin crouches at the door. Its desire is for you, but you are to rule over it.
verses.meaning: God warned Cain that temptation lurks close and wants control. You’re called to master it, not obey it.
verses.kjv: If thou doest well, shalt thou not be accepted? and if thou doest not well, sin lieth at the door. And unto thee shall be his desire, and thou shalt rule over him.

verses.text: God saw everything that he had made, and, behold, it was very good. There was evening and there was morning, a sixth day.
verses.meaning: When God looked over everything he had made, people included, he called it very good. That includes you.
verses.kjv: And God saw every thing that he had made, and, behold, it was very good. And the evening and the morning were the sixth day.

verses.text: You prepare a table before me in the presence of my enemies. You anoint my head with oil. My cup runs over.
verses.meaning: God sets a table for you even when trouble is near. His care doesn’t wait for every enemy to leave.
verses.kjv: Thou preparest a table before me in the presence of mine enemies: thou anointest my head with oil; my cup runneth over.

verses.text: The LORD God said, “It is not good for the man to be alone. I will make him a helper comparable to him.”
verses.meaning: From the very start, God said being alone isn’t good. You were made for companionship.
verses.kjv: And the LORD God said, It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him an help meet for him.

verses.text: He left that place, and dug another well. They didn’t argue over that one. So he called it Rehoboth. He said, “For now the LORD has made room for us, and we will be fruitful in the land.”
verses.meaning: Isaac kept moving on instead of fighting over wells, until God made room. Not every fight needs winning.
verses.kjv: And he removed from thence, and digged another well; and for that they strove not: and he called the name of it Rehoboth; and he said, For now the LORD hath made room for us, and we shall be fruitful in the land.

verses.text: David was greatly distressed, for the people spoke of stoning him, because the souls of all the people were grieved, every man for his sons and for his daughters; but David strengthened himself in the LORD his God.
verses.meaning: When everything fell apart and even his own people turned on him, David found his footing again in God.
verses.kjv: And David was greatly distressed; for the people spake of stoning him, because the soul of all the people was grieved, every man for his sons and for his daughters: but David encouraged himself in the LORD his God.

verses.text: Trust in him at all times, you people. Pour out your heart before him. God is a refuge for us. Selah.
verses.meaning: You don’t have to hold it all in. Tell God everything on your heart; he’s a safe place to land.
verses.kjv: Trust in him at all times; ye people, pour out your heart before him: God is a refuge for us. Selah.

verses.text: Let them praise the LORD for his loving kindness, for his wonderful deeds to the children of men!
verses.meaning: After each rescue story in this psalm comes the same refrain: when God helps you, tell him thanks.
verses.kjv: Oh that men would praise the LORD for his goodness, and for his wonderful works to the children of men!

verses.text: The LORD passed by before him, and proclaimed, “The LORD! The LORD, a merciful and gracious God, slow to anger, and abundant in loving kindness and truth…”
verses.meaning: When God described himself to Moses, he led with mercy: patient, gracious and full of faithful love.
verses.kjv: And the LORD passed by before him, and proclaimed, The LORD, The LORD God, merciful and gracious, longsuffering, and abundant in goodness and truth…

verses.text: I will make of you a great nation. I will bless you and make your name great. You will be a blessing.
verses.meaning: God blessed Abram so he could bless others. What God gives you is meant to flow on to someone else.
verses.kjv: And I will make of thee a great nation, and I will bless thee, and make thy name great; and thou shalt be a blessing…

verses.text: Behold, because the LORD has given you the Sabbath, therefore he gives you on the sixth day the bread of two days. Everyone stay in his place. Let no one go out of his place on the seventh day.
verses.meaning: God sent extra bread the day before the Sabbath so his people could truly stop. He provides for your rest.
verses.kjv: See, for that the LORD hath given you the sabbath, therefore he giveth you on the sixth day the bread of two days; abide ye every man in his place, let no man go out of his place on the seventh day.

verses.text: You, who have shown us many and bitter troubles, you will let me live. You will bring us up again from the depths of the earth.
verses.meaning: Even after many bitter troubles, God can bring you back up from the lowest place and give you life again.
verses.kjv: Thou, which hast shewed me great and sore troubles, shalt quicken me again, and shalt bring me up again from the depths of the earth.

verses.text: “‘You shall tell Joseph, “Now please forgive the disobedience of your brothers, and their sin, because they did evil to you.”’ Now, please forgive the disobedience of the servants of the God of your father.” Joseph wept when they spoke to him.
verses.meaning: Joseph’s brothers finally asked him to forgive the evil they’d done, and he wept. Some apologies take years.
verses.kjv: So shall ye say unto Joseph, Forgive, I pray thee now, the trespass of thy brethren, and their sin; for they did unto thee evil: and now, we pray thee, forgive the trespass of the servants of the God of thy father. And Joseph wept when they spake unto him.

verses.text: Caleb stilled the people before Moses, and said, “Let’s go up at once, and possess it; for we are well able to overcome it!”
verses.meaning: Most of the spies saw only giants, but Caleb saw God’s promise. Faith moves forward when others hang back.
verses.kjv: And Caleb stilled the people before Moses, and said, Let us go up at once, and possess it; for we are well able to overcome it.

verses.text: No one is greater in this house than I am, and he has not kept back anything from me but you, because you are his wife. How then can I do this great wickedness, and sin against God?
verses.meaning: Joseph turned down temptation by remembering whom it would really wrong: God. That thought can stop you too.
verses.kjv: There is none greater in this house than I; neither hath he kept back any thing from me but thee, because thou art his wife: how then can I do this great wickedness, and sin against God?

verses.text: The LORD God formed man from the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul.
verses.meaning: You’re made of dust and the breath of God. Your life began as his gift, up close and personal.
verses.kjv: And the LORD God formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul.

verses.text: I am the LORD, your God, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt. Open your mouth wide, and I will fill it.
verses.meaning: The God who brought his people out of Egypt longs to fill you. Come to him hungry and trust his care.
verses.kjv: I am the LORD thy God, which brought thee out of the land of Egypt: open thy mouth wide, and I will fill it.

verses.text: He kissed all his brothers, and wept on them. After that his brothers talked with him.
verses.meaning: After years of hurt, Joseph wept over the brothers who betrayed him, and they finally talked again.
verses.kjv: Moreover he kissed all his brethren, and wept upon them: and after that his brethren talked with him.

verses.text: The LORD said to him, “Peace be to you! Don’t be afraid. You shall not die.” Then Gideon built an altar there to the LORD, and called it “The LORD is Peace.” To this day it is still in Ophrah of the Abiezrites.
verses.meaning: Terrified Gideon heard God say “Peace,” then named the spot after it. God’s peace can meet you in your fear.
verses.kjv: And the LORD said unto him, Peace be unto thee; fear not: thou shalt not die. Then Gideon built an altar there unto the LORD, and called it Jehovah-shalom: unto this day it is yet in Ophrah of the Abi-ezrites.

verses.text: Jonathan, Saul’s son, arose and went to David into the woods, and strengthened his hand in God.
verses.meaning: Jonathan went looking for David in hiding and pointed him back to God. Be that kind of friend to someone.
verses.kjv: And Jonathan Saul’s son arose, and went to David into the wood, and strengthened his hand in God.

verses.text: When my spirit was overwhelmed within me, you knew my route. On the path in which I walk, they have hidden a snare for me.
verses.meaning: Even when you’re too overwhelmed to think straight, God knows exactly where you are and where you’re headed.
verses.kjv: When my spirit was overwhelmed within me, then thou knewest my path. In the way wherein I walked have they privily laid a snare for me.

verses.text: What will I give to the LORD for all his benefits toward me?
verses.meaning: When you count how much God has given you, the natural question is how to give something back.
verses.kjv: What shall I render unto the LORD for all his benefits toward me?

verses.text: You shall love the LORD your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your might.
verses.meaning: Love for God isn’t one slice of your life. It’s meant to fill your heart, your soul and your strength.
verses.kjv: And thou shalt love the LORD thy God with all thine heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy might.

verses.text: Now, Israel, what does the LORD your God require of you, but to fear the LORD your God, to walk in all his ways, to love him, and to serve the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your soul…
verses.meaning: God’s ask is simple to say and big to live: honor him, follow him, love him and serve with your whole self.
verses.kjv: And now, Israel, what doth the LORD thy God require of thee, but to fear the LORD thy God, to walk in all his ways, and to love him, and to serve the LORD thy God with all thy heart and with all thy soul…

verses.text: Six days you shall do your work, and on the seventh day you shall rest, that your ox and your donkey may have rest, and the son of your servant, and the alien may be refreshed.
verses.meaning: God’s day of rest wasn’t just for the boss: workers, outsiders and even animals got to breathe.
verses.kjv: Six days thou shalt do thy work, and on the seventh day thou shalt rest: that thine ox and thine ass may rest, and the son of thy handmaid, and the stranger, may be refreshed.

verses.text: For you are my hope, Lord GOD, my confidence from my youth.
verses.meaning: The writer had trusted God since childhood. Whatever your age, God can be your hope and confidence.
verses.kjv: For thou art my hope, O Lord GOD: thou art my trust from my youth.

verses.text: “Please pardon the iniquity of this people according to the greatness of your loving kindness, and just as you have forgiven this people, from Egypt even until now.” The LORD said, “I have pardoned according to your word…”
verses.meaning: Moses asked God to forgive his people again, as he had so many times before, and God answered: pardoned.
verses.kjv: Pardon, I beseech thee, the iniquity of this people according unto the greatness of thy mercy, and as thou hast forgiven this people, from Egypt even until now. And the LORD said, I have pardoned according to thy word…

verses.text: David said, “The LORD, who delivered me out of the paw of the lion and out of the paw of the bear, will deliver me out of the hand of this Philistine.” Saul said to David, “Go! The LORD will be with you.”
verses.meaning: David remembered how God had helped him before. Past faithfulness can give you nerve to face today’s giant.
verses.kjv: David said moreover, The LORD that delivered me out of the paw of the lion, and out of the paw of the bear, he will deliver me out of the hand of this Philistine. And Saul said unto David, Go, and the LORD be with thee.

verses.text: Give your servant therefore an understanding heart to judge your people, that I may discern between good and evil; for who is able to judge this great people of yours?
verses.meaning: Solomon could have asked for anything. He asked for a heart that listens and can tell right from wrong.
verses.kjv: Give therefore thy servant an understanding heart to judge thy people, that I may discern between good and bad: for who is able to judge this thy so great a people?

verses.text: He said, “Your name will no longer be called Jacob, but Israel; for you have fought with God and with men, and have prevailed.”
verses.meaning: After a night of wrestling with God, Jacob the schemer walked away with a new name. God can remake you too.
verses.kjv: And he said, Thy name shall be called no more Jacob, but Israel: for as a prince hast thou power with God and with men, and hast prevailed.

verses.text: For the LORD God is a sun and a shield. The LORD will give grace and glory. He withholds no good thing from those who walk blamelessly.
verses.meaning: God isn’t stingy with you. He gives grace and holds back nothing truly good from those who walk with him.
verses.kjv: For the LORD God is a sun and shield: the LORD will give grace and glory: no good thing will he withhold from them that walk uprightly.

verses.text: Honor your father and your mother, that your days may be long in the land which the LORD your God gives you.
verses.meaning: Honoring your parents is one of the Ten Commandments. Respect and care for them matter at every age.
verses.kjv: Honour thy father and thy mother: that thy days may be long upon the land which the LORD thy God giveth thee.

verses.text: Then Eli answered, “Go in peace; and may the God of Israel grant your petition that you have asked of him.” She said, “Let your servant find favor in your sight.” So the woman went her way and ate; and her facial expression wasn’t sad any more.
verses.meaning: Hannah still had no answer, yet after pouring out her heart to God she left in peace, no longer sad.
verses.kjv: Then Eli answered and said, Go in peace: and the God of Israel grant thee thy petition that thou hast asked of him. And she said, Let thine handmaid find grace in thy sight. So the woman went her way, and did eat, and her countenance was no more sad.

verses.text: For they all would have made us afraid, saying, “Their hands will be weakened from the work, that it not be done.” But now, strengthen my hands.
verses.meaning: Opponents tried to scare Nehemiah into quitting the wall. His answer was a quick prayer: God, make me strong.
verses.kjv: For they all made us afraid, saying, Their hands shall be weakened from the work, that it be not done. Now therefore, O God, strengthen my hands.

verses.text: But I trust in you, LORD. I said, “You are my God.” My times are in your hand. Deliver me from the hand of my enemies, and from those who persecute me.
verses.meaning: You don’t have to control what comes next. Your days, and every hour in them, rest in God’s hands.
verses.kjv: But I trusted in thee, O LORD: I said, Thou art my God. My times are in thy hand: deliver me from the hand of mine enemies, and from them that persecute me.

verses.text: The lines have fallen to me in pleasant places. Yes, I have a good inheritance.
verses.meaning: David looked at his life and called it a good inheritance. Gratitude helps you see your own portion that way.
verses.kjv: The lines are fallen unto me in pleasant places; yea, I have a goodly heritage.

verses.text: Know therefore that the LORD your God himself is God, the faithful God, who keeps covenant and loving kindness to a thousand generations with those who love him and keep his commandments…
verses.meaning: God keeps his promises and his love going for a thousand generations. He doesn’t give up on his people.
verses.kjv: Know therefore that the LORD thy God, he is God, the faithful God, which keepeth covenant and mercy with them that love him and keep his commandments to a thousand generations…

verses.text: The LORD looked at him, and said, “Go in this your might, and save Israel from the hand of Midian. Haven’t I sent you?”
verses.meaning: Gideon felt weak and overlooked, but God sent him anyway. When God sends you, what you have is enough.
verses.kjv: And the LORD looked upon him, and said, Go in this thy might, and thou shalt save Israel from the hand of the Midianites: have not I sent thee?

verses.text: Six days you shall work, but on the seventh day you shall rest: in plowing time and in harvest you shall rest.
verses.meaning: Even in the busiest season, God said stop one day in seven. Rest isn’t only for when the work is done.
verses.kjv: Six days thou shalt work, but on the seventh day thou shalt rest: in earing time and in harvest thou shalt rest.

verses.text: Now, Lord, what do I wait for? My hope is in you.
verses.meaning: When everything else feels uncertain, you can say it plainly: God, my hope is in you.
verses.kjv: And now, Lord, what wait I for? my hope is in thee.

verses.text: David said to Nathan, “I have sinned against the LORD.” Nathan said to David, “The LORD also has put away your sin. You will not die.”
verses.meaning: When David stopped hiding and owned what he did, forgiveness came right away. Honesty opens the door.
verses.kjv: And David said unto Nathan, I have sinned against the LORD. And Nathan said unto David, The LORD also hath put away thy sin; thou shalt not die.

verses.text: Then David said to the Philistine, “You come to me with a sword, with a spear, and with a javelin; but I come to you in the name of the LORD of Armies, the God of the armies of Israel, whom you have defied.”
verses.meaning: Goliath came with every weapon he had. David came trusting God’s name, and that was more than enough.
verses.kjv: Then said David to the Philistine, Thou comest to me with a sword, and with a spear, and with a shield: but I come to thee in the name of the LORD of hosts, the God of the armies of Israel, whom thou hast defied.

verses.text: Elijah came near to all the people, and said, “How long will you waver between the two sides? If the LORD is God, follow him; but if Baal, then follow him.” The people didn’t say a word.
verses.meaning: Elijah’s challenge still lands: stop hovering between two loyalties. If God is God, follow him fully.
verses.kjv: And Elijah came unto all the people, and said, How long halt ye between two opinions? if the LORD be God, follow him: but if Baal, then follow him. And the people answered him not a word.

verses.text: You have seen what I did to the Egyptians, and how I bore you on eagles’ wings, and brought you to myself.
verses.meaning: God carried his people out of slavery like an eagle carries its young, to bring them close to himself.
verses.kjv: Ye have seen what I did unto the Egyptians, and how I bare you on eagles’ wings, and brought you unto myself.

verses.text: He causes the grass to grow for the livestock, and plants for man to cultivate, that he may produce food out of the earth: wine that makes the heart of man glad, oil to make his face to shine, and bread that strengthens man’s heart.
verses.meaning: Every meal and every glad moment at the table traces back to God, who makes the earth grow food.
verses.kjv: He causeth the grass to grow for the cattle, and herb for the service of man: that he may bring forth food out of the earth; And wine that maketh glad the heart of man, and oil to make his face to shine, and bread which strengtheneth man’s heart.

verses.text: If you meet your enemy’s ox or his donkey going astray, you shall surely bring it back to him again. If you see the donkey of him who hates you fallen down under his burden, don’t leave him. You shall surely help him with it.
verses.meaning: Help even people who dislike you when they’re in trouble. Kindness doesn’t wait for friendship.
verses.kjv: If thou meet thine enemy’s ox or his ass going astray, thou shalt surely bring it back to him again. If thou see the ass of him that hateth thee lying under his burden, and wouldest forbear to help him, thou shalt surely help with him.

verses.text: He prepared a great feast for them. After they ate and drank, he sent them away and they went to their master. So the bands of Syria stopped raiding the land of Israel.
verses.meaning: Instead of killing captured enemy soldiers, Israel fed them and sent them home. Then the raids stopped.
verses.kjv: And he prepared great provision for them: and when they had eaten and drunk, he sent them away, and they went to their master. So the bands of Syria came no more into the land of Israel.

verses.text: Your bars will be iron and bronze. As your days, so your strength will be.
verses.meaning: God doesn’t hand you all your strength in advance. He gives enough for each day, as each day comes.
verses.kjv: Thy shoes shall be iron and brass; and as thy days, so shall thy strength be.

verses.text: Turn to me, and have mercy on me, for I am desolate and afflicted. The troubles of my heart are enlarged. Oh bring me out of my distresses.
verses.meaning: When worry piles up and you feel alone, you can simply ask God to turn toward you and pull you out.
verses.kjv: Turn thee unto me, and have mercy upon me; for I am desolate and afflicted. The troubles of my heart are enlarged: O bring thou me out of my distresses.

verses.text: Many, LORD, my God, are the wonderful works which you have done, and your thoughts which are toward us. They can’t be declared back to you. If I would declare and speak of them, they are more than can be counted.
verses.meaning: Try counting God’s kindness to you and you’ll run out of numbers before you run out of reasons.
verses.kjv: Many, O LORD my God, are thy wonderful works which thou hast done, and thy thoughts which are to us-ward: they cannot be reckoned up in order unto thee: if I would declare and speak of them, they are more than can be numbered.

verses.text: The LORD your God will circumcise your heart, and the heart of your offspring, to love the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your soul, that you may live.
verses.meaning: God himself softens your heart so you can love him fully. Love for God starts as his gift to you.
verses.kjv: And the LORD thy God will circumcise thine heart, and the heart of thy seed, to love the LORD thy God with all thine heart, and with all thy soul, that thou mayest live.

verses.text: The LORD came, and stood, and called as at other times, “Samuel! Samuel!” Then Samuel said, “Speak; for your servant hears.”
verses.meaning: Young Samuel didn’t need a big speech, just open ears. “I’m listening, Lord” is a great way to begin.
verses.kjv: And the LORD came, and stood, and called as at other times, Samuel, Samuel. Then Samuel answered, Speak; for thy servant heareth.

verses.text: They set forward from the Mount of the LORD three days’ journey. The ark of the LORD’s covenant went before them three days’ journey, to seek out a resting place for them.
verses.meaning: On Israel’s journey, God went on ahead to find them a place to rest. He plans for your rest too.
verses.kjv: And they departed from the mount of the LORD three days’ journey: and the ark of the covenant of the LORD went before them in the three days’ journey, to search out a resting place for them.

verses.text: Our soul has waited for the LORD. He is our help and our shield. For our heart rejoices in him, because we have trusted in his holy name. Let your loving kindness be on us, LORD, since we have hoped in you.
verses.meaning: Hoping in God isn’t wishful thinking. He’s your help and shield, and his love rests over you.
verses.kjv: Our soul waiteth for the LORD: he is our help and our shield. For our heart shall rejoice in him, because we have trusted in his holy name. Let thy mercy, O LORD, be upon us, according as we hope in thee.

verses.text: Don’t remember the sins of my youth, nor my transgressions. Remember me according to your loving kindness, for your goodness’ sake, LORD.
verses.meaning: You can ask God not to see you through your old mistakes, but through his steady love and goodness.
verses.kjv: Remember not the sins of my youth, nor my transgressions: according to thy mercy remember thou me for thy goodness’ sake, O LORD.

verses.text: Be courageous, and let’s be strong for our people and for the cities of our God; and may the LORD do what seems good to him.
verses.meaning: Do your part bravely for the people you love, then leave the outcome in God’s hands.
verses.kjv: Be of good courage, and let us play the men for our people, and for the cities of our God: and the LORD do that which seemeth him good.

verses.text: I sent messengers to them, saying, “I am doing a great work, so that I can’t come down. Why should the work cease while I leave it and come down to you?”
verses.meaning: Nehemiah’s enemies kept trying to pull him off the job. He said no: the work mattered too much. Guard yours.
verses.kjv: And I sent messengers unto them, saying, I am doing a great work, so that I cannot come down: why should the work cease, whilst I leave it, and come down to you?

verses.text: For you are a holy people to the LORD your God. The LORD your God has chosen you to be a people for his own possession, above all peoples who are on the face of the earth.
verses.meaning: Spoken to Israel: God chose them as his own, on purpose. Belonging to God sets you apart.
verses.kjv: For thou art an holy people unto the LORD thy God: the LORD thy God hath chosen thee to be a special people unto himself, above all people that are upon the face of the earth.

verses.text: For he satisfies the longing soul. He fills the hungry soul with good.
verses.meaning: Your deepest hunger isn’t only in your stomach. God knows how to satisfy the longing in your soul.
verses.kjv: For he satisfieth the longing soul, and filleth the hungry soul with goodness.

verses.text: ‘You shall rise up before the gray head and honor the face of the elderly; and you shall fear your God. I am the LORD.’
verses.meaning: Stand when an older person enters and treat them with honor. Respecting elders is part of honoring God.
verses.kjv: Thou shalt rise up before the hoary head, and honour the face of the old man, and fear thy God: I am the LORD.

verses.text: So the Levites calmed all the people, saying, “Hold your peace, for the day is holy. Don’t be grieved.”
verses.meaning: As people wept over their failures, the leaders calmed them: this was a holy day for joy, not despair.
verses.kjv: So the Levites stilled all the people, saying, Hold your peace, for the day is holy; neither be ye grieved.

verses.text: Then he answered and spoke to me, saying, “This is the LORD’s word to Zerubbabel, saying, ‘Not by might, nor by power, but by my Spirit,’ says the LORD of Armies.”
verses.meaning: God’s work doesn’t depend on your muscle or your clout. His Spirit gets done what you never could alone.
verses.kjv: Then he answered and spake unto me, saying, This is the word of the LORD unto Zerubbabel, saying, Not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit, saith the LORD of hosts.

verses.text: If I say, “Surely the darkness will overwhelm me. The light around me will be night,” even the darkness doesn’t hide from you, but the night shines as the day. The darkness is like light to you.
verses.meaning: Even when darkness feels like it’s closing in, it isn’t dark to God. He sees you clearly at night.
verses.kjv: If I say, Surely the darkness shall cover me; even the night shall be light about me. Yea, the darkness hideth not from thee; but the night shineth as the day: the darkness and the light are both alike to thee.

verses.text: But I trust in your loving kindness. My heart rejoices in your salvation. I will sing to the LORD, because he has been good to me.
verses.meaning: This psalm begins with “How long?” and ends with a song. Remembering God’s goodness can turn a prayer around.
verses.kjv: But I have trusted in thy mercy; my heart shall rejoice in thy salvation. I will sing unto the LORD, because he hath dealt bountifully with me.

verses.text: I will be glad and rejoice in your loving kindness, for you have seen my affliction. You have known my soul in adversities.
verses.meaning: God has seen your hardest days and knows what your soul went through. You can be glad in his love.
verses.kjv: I will be glad and rejoice in thy mercy: for thou hast considered my trouble; thou hast known my soul in adversities…

verses.text: Only fear the LORD, and serve him in truth with all your heart; for consider what great things he has done for you.
verses.meaning: Serve God sincerely and wholeheartedly. Looking back at all he’s done for you is fuel for it.
verses.kjv: Only fear the LORD, and serve him in truth with all your heart: for consider how great things he hath done for you.

verses.text: I will come down and talk with you there. I will take of the Spirit which is on you, and will put it on them; and they shall bear the burden of the people with you, that you don’t bear it yourself alone.
verses.meaning: God didn’t leave Moses to carry everyone alone. He gave him helpers to share the weight.
verses.kjv: And I will come down and talk with thee there: and I will take of the spirit which is upon thee, and will put it upon them; and they shall bear the burden of the people with thee, that thou bear it not thyself alone.

verses.text: He heals the broken in heart, and binds up their wounds.
verses.meaning: God doesn’t ignore broken hearts. He tends to them gently, like someone bandaging a wound.
verses.kjv: He healeth the broken in heart, and bindeth up their wounds.

verses.text: I acknowledged my sin to you. I didn’t hide my iniquity. I said, I will confess my transgressions to the LORD, and you forgave the iniquity of my sin. Selah.
verses.meaning: Hiding sin wears you down. The moment you tell God the truth about it, he forgives.
verses.kjv: I acknowledged my sin unto thee, and mine iniquity have I not hid. I said, I will confess my transgressions unto the LORD; and thou forgavest the iniquity of my sin. Selah.

verses.text: David said to Solomon his son, “Be strong and courageous, and do it. Don’t be afraid, nor be dismayed, for the LORD God, even my God, is with you. He will not fail you nor forsake you, until all the work for the service of the LORD’s house is finished.”
verses.meaning: David told Solomon to take on the huge task ahead without fear: God won’t leave you before the work is done.
verses.kjv: And David said to Solomon his son, Be strong and of good courage, and do it: fear not, nor be dismayed: for the LORD God, even my God, will be with thee; he will not fail thee, nor forsake thee, until thou hast finished all the work for the service of the house of the LORD.

verses.text: I made a covenant with my eyes; how then should I look lustfully at a young woman?
verses.meaning: Job made a firm deal with his own eyes about where they would look. A decision made ahead of time helps.
verses.kjv: I made a covenant with mine eyes; why then should I think upon a maid?

verses.text: He found him in a desert land, in the waste howling wilderness. He surrounded him. He cared for him. He kept him as the apple of his eye.
verses.meaning: God found his people lost in a wasteland and guarded them like the most precious thing he had.
verses.kjv: He found him in a desert land, and in the waste howling wilderness; he led him about, he instructed him, he kept him as the apple of his eye.

verses.text: He has given food to those who fear him. He always remembers his covenant.
verses.meaning: God feeds his people and never forgets his promises. His past faithfulness is your reason to trust him today.
verses.kjv: He hath given meat unto them that fear him: he will ever be mindful of his covenant.

verses.text: The stranger who lives as a foreigner with you shall be to you as the native-born among you, and you shall love him as yourself; for you lived as foreigners in the land of Egypt. I am the LORD your God.
verses.meaning: Treat the newcomer in your community as one of your own, and love them the way you love yourself.
verses.kjv: But the stranger that dwelleth with you shall be unto you as one born among you, and thou shalt love him as thyself; for ye were strangers in the land of Egypt: I am the LORD your God.

verses.text: For Mordecai the Jew was next to King Ahasuerus, and great among the Jews and accepted by the multitude of his brothers, seeking the good of his people and speaking peace to all his descendants.
verses.meaning: Mordecai rose high but kept working for his people’s good. Influence is best used to build peace.
verses.kjv: For Mordecai the Jew was next unto king Ahasuerus, and great among the Jews, and accepted of the multitude of his brethren, seeking the wealth of his people, and speaking peace to all his seed.

verses.text: For a righteous man falls seven times and rises up again, but the wicked are overthrown by calamity.
verses.meaning: Getting knocked down again and again doesn’t define you. People who belong to God keep getting back up.
verses.kjv: For a just man falleth seven times, and riseth up again: but the wicked shall fall into mischief.

verses.text: In the day of my trouble I will call on you, for you will answer me.
verses.meaning: On your hardest day, you can call on God with confidence. He’s the kind of God who answers.
verses.kjv: In the day of my trouble I will call upon thee: for thou wilt answer me.

verses.text: Let’s come before his presence with thanksgiving. Let’s extol him with songs!
verses.meaning: Before you bring God your requests, try bringing him your thanks. It’s a great way to begin praying.
verses.kjv: Let us come before his presence with thanksgiving, and make a joyful noise unto him with psalms.

verses.text: Your loving kindness, LORD, is in the heavens. Your faithfulness reaches to the skies.
verses.meaning: God’s love and faithfulness are bigger than the sky. However far you look, they reach farther.
verses.kjv: Thy mercy, O LORD, is in the heavens; and thy faithfulness reacheth unto the clouds.

verses.text: For Ezra had set his heart to seek the LORD’s law, and to do it, and to teach statutes and ordinances in Israel.
verses.meaning: Ezra set his heart on three things in order: study God’s word, live it, then teach it. A solid life plan.
verses.kjv: For Ezra had prepared his heart to seek the law of the LORD, and to do it, and to teach in Israel statutes and judgments.

verses.text: You shall remember that you were a servant in the land of Egypt, and the LORD your God brought you out of there by a mighty hand and by an outstretched arm. Therefore the LORD your God commanded you to keep the Sabbath day.
verses.meaning: Sabbath is a reminder that you’re not a slave anymore. God set his people free, and rest celebrates it.
verses.kjv: And remember that thou wast a servant in the land of Egypt, and that the LORD thy God brought thee out thence through a mighty hand and by a stretched out arm: therefore the LORD thy God commanded thee to keep the sabbath day.

verses.text: For the needy shall not always be forgotten, nor the hope of the poor perish forever.
verses.meaning: People in need may feel forgotten, but God hasn’t forgotten them. Their hope won’t die.
verses.kjv: For the needy shall not alway be forgotten: the expectation of the poor shall not perish for ever.

verses.text: Purify me with hyssop, and I will be clean. Wash me, and I will be whiter than snow.
verses.meaning: Written after David’s worst failure: no stain is so deep that God can’t wash it completely clean.
verses.kjv: Purge me with hyssop, and I shall be clean: wash me, and I shall be whiter than snow.

verses.text: “Go, gather together all the Jews who are present in Susa, and fast for me, and neither eat nor drink three days, night or day. I and my maidens will also fast the same way. Then I will go in to the king, which is against the law; and if I perish, I perish.”
verses.meaning: After fasting and prayer, Esther chose to do the right thing even if it cost her everything.
verses.kjv: Go, gather together all the Jews that are present in Shushan, and fast ye for me, and neither eat nor drink three days, night or day: I also and my maidens will fast likewise; and so will I go in unto the king, which is not according to the law: and if I perish, I perish.

verses.text: But his delight is in the LORD’s law. On his law he meditates day and night.
verses.meaning: Joy comes from soaking in God’s word, turning it over day and night, not just glancing at it.
verses.kjv: But his delight is in the law of the LORD; and in his law doth he meditate day and night.

verses.text: But the LORD said to Samuel, “Don’t look on his face, or on the height of his stature, because I have rejected him; for I don’t see as man sees. For man looks at the outward appearance, but the LORD looks at the heart.”
verses.meaning: People size you up by how you look. God looks past all of that, straight to your heart.
verses.kjv: But the LORD said unto Samuel, Look not on his countenance, or on the height of his stature; because I have refused him: for the Lord seeth not as man seeth; for man looketh on the outward appearance, but the LORD looketh on the heart.

verses.text: Who executes justice for the oppressed; who gives food to the hungry. The LORD frees the prisoners.
verses.meaning: God takes the side of the hungry and the oppressed. Caring for people in need is close to his heart.
verses.kjv: Which executeth judgment for the oppressed: which giveth food to the hungry. The LORD looseth the prisoners…

verses.text: For the poor will never cease out of the land. Therefore I command you to surely open your hand to your brother, to your needy, and to your poor, in your land.
verses.meaning: There will always be people in need near you. God asks you to keep your hand open to them, not closed.
verses.kjv: For the poor shall never cease out of the land: therefore I command thee, saying, Thou shalt open thine hand wide unto thy brother, to thy poor, and to thy needy, in thy land.

verses.text: Depart from evil, and do good. Seek peace, and pursue it.
verses.meaning: Peace rarely just happens. Turn from what harms, do good, and go after peace like it matters.
verses.kjv: Depart from evil, and do good; seek peace, and pursue it.

verses.text: He will corrupt those who do wickedly against the covenant by flatteries; but the people who know their God will be strong and take action.
verses.meaning: When pressure comes to make you bend, people who truly know God find the strength to stand firm and act.
verses.kjv: And such as do wickedly against the covenant shall he corrupt by flatteries: but the people that do know their God shall be strong, and do exploits.

verses.text: But I am poor and needy. May the Lord think about me. You are my help and my deliverer. Don’t delay, my God.
verses.meaning: You can pray honestly when you feel needy and small: God, think of me, help me, and please don’t wait.
verses.kjv: But I am poor and needy; yet the Lord thinketh upon me: thou art my help and my deliverer; make no tarrying, O my God.

verses.text: Every day I will praise you. I will extol your name forever and ever.
verses.meaning: Praise isn’t only for Sundays or big wins. Make thanking God a daily habit, as regular as breakfast.
verses.kjv: Every day will I bless thee; and I will praise thy name for ever and ever.

verses.text: But as for me, I am like a green olive tree in God’s house. I trust in God’s loving kindness forever and ever.
verses.meaning: Like an olive tree rooted near God’s house, you can stay green by trusting a love that never runs out.
verses.kjv: But I am like a green olive tree in the house of God: I trust in the mercy of God for ever and ever.

verses.text: I know that you can do all things, and that no purpose of yours can be restrained.
verses.meaning: After all his questions, Job landed here: God can do anything, and no plan of his can be stopped.
verses.kjv: I know that thou canst do every thing, and that no thought can be withholden from thee.

verses.text: About Benjamin he said, “The beloved of the LORD will dwell in safety by him. He covers him all day long. He dwells between his shoulders.”
verses.meaning: Picture being so loved by God that you rest safe beside him, carried close all day long.
verses.kjv: And of Benjamin he said, The beloved of the LORD shall dwell in safety by him; and the Lord shall cover him all the day long, and he shall dwell between his shoulders.

verses.text: You will show me the path of life. In your presence is fullness of joy. In your right hand there are pleasures forever more.
verses.meaning: God shows you the path that leads to real life, and in his presence there’s joy that never runs out.
verses.kjv: Thou wilt shew me the path of life: in thy presence is fulness of joy; at thy right hand there are pleasures for evermore.

verses.text: The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit. O God, you will not despise a broken and contrite heart.
verses.meaning: God isn’t after a flawless performance. He welcomes a heart that’s honest and broken over its wrongs.
verses.kjv: The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit: a broken and a contrite heart, O God, thou wilt not despise.

verses.text: Though an army should encamp against me, my heart shall not fear. Though war should rise against me, even then I will be confident.
verses.meaning: Even if trouble lines up against you like an army, your heart can stay steady because God is with you.
verses.kjv: Though an host should encamp against me, my heart shall not fear: though war should rise against me, in this will I be confident.

verses.text: LORD, in the morning you will hear my voice. In the morning I will lay my requests before you, and will watch expectantly.
verses.meaning: Before the feed, bring God your morning requests, then watch for his answer. Mornings set the tone.
verses.kjv: My voice shalt thou hear in the morning, O LORD; in the morning will I direct my prayer unto thee, and will look up.

verses.text: The Spirit of God has made me, and the breath of the Almighty gives me life.
verses.meaning: Your life isn’t random. God’s own Spirit made you, and his breath keeps you going every day.
verses.kjv: The Spirit of God hath made me, and the breath of the Almighty hath given me life.

verses.text: Who covers the sky with clouds, who prepares rain for the earth, who makes grass grow on the mountains. He provides food for the livestock, and for the young ravens when they call.
verses.meaning: The God who sends rain and feeds baby ravens when they cry is paying attention when you call too.
verses.kjv: Who covereth the heaven with clouds, who prepareth rain for the earth, who maketh grass to grow upon the mountains. He giveth to the beast his food, and to the young ravens which cry.

verses.text: When you reap your harvest in your field, and have forgotten a sheaf in the field, you shall not go again to get it. It shall be for the foreigner, for the fatherless, and for the widow, that the LORD your God may bless you in all the work of your hands.
verses.meaning: God told farmers to leave some harvest for those in need. Leave a little margin in your life for others.
verses.kjv: When thou cuttest down thine harvest in thy field, and hast forgot a sheaf in the field, thou shalt not go again to fetch it: it shall be for the stranger, for the fatherless, and for the widow: that the LORD thy God may bless thee in all the work of thine hands.

verses.text: But the humble shall inherit the land, and shall delight themselves in the abundance of peace.
verses.meaning: The humble can look like they’re losing, but God says they’ll end up enjoying peace in full.
verses.kjv: But the meek shall inherit the earth; and shall delight themselves in the abundance of peace.

verses.text: Both riches and honor come from you, and you rule over all! In your hand is power and might! It is in your hand to make great, and to give strength to all!
verses.meaning: Every bit of strength you have is on loan from God, who has the power to lift up anyone he chooses.
verses.kjv: Both riches and honour come of thee, and thou reignest over all; and in thine hand is power and might; and in thine hand it is to make great, and to give strength unto all.

verses.text: Out of my distress, I called on the LORD. The LORD answered me with freedom.
verses.meaning: Distress can make life feel cramped and tight. When you call on God, he answers by setting you free.
verses.kjv: I called upon the LORD in distress: the LORD answered me, and set me in a large place.

verses.text: Whoever offers the sacrifice of thanksgiving glorifies me, and prepares his way so that I will show God’s salvation to him.
verses.meaning: God values a thankful heart more than a show of religion. Gratitude honors him and opens the way to his help.
verses.kjv: Whoso offereth praise glorifieth me: and to him that ordereth his conversation aright will I shew the salvation of God.

verses.text: Satisfy us in the morning with your loving kindness, that we may rejoice and be glad all our days.
verses.meaning: A prayer for every morning: let God’s love fill you up first, so joy can last through all your days.
verses.kjv: O satisfy us early with thy mercy; that we may rejoice and be glad all our days.

verses.text: The LORD will fulfill that which concerns me. Your loving kindness, LORD, endures forever. Don’t forsake the works of your own hands.
verses.meaning: God won’t leave his work in you half done. You’re something his hands made, and he keeps at it.
verses.kjv: The LORD will perfect that which concerneth me: thy mercy, O LORD, endureth for ever: forsake not the works of thine own hands.

verses.text: The king and all the people who were with him arrived weary; and he refreshed himself there.
verses.meaning: After a day of insults on a hard road, David stopped to recover. Even kings need to rest.
verses.kjv: And the king, and all the people that were with him, came weary, and refreshed themselves there.

verses.text: You are my hiding place and my shield. I hope in your word.
verses.meaning: When you need somewhere to hide, God is your shelter, and his word gives you something to hope in.
verses.kjv: Thou art my hiding place and my shield: I hope in thy word.

verses.text: Sins overwhelmed me, but you atoned for our transgressions.
verses.meaning: When your sins feel like too much, remember God has already dealt with them. They don’t win.
verses.kjv: Iniquities prevail against me: as for our transgressions, thou shalt purge them away.

verses.text: Be strong, and let your heart take courage, all you who hope in the LORD.
verses.meaning: Hoping in God isn’t passive. It gives you a backbone and a brave heart for whatever comes next.
verses.kjv: Be of good courage, and he shall strengthen your heart, all ye that hope in the LORD.

verses.text: My eyes are ever on the LORD, for he will pluck my feet out of the net.
verses.meaning: Keep your eyes on the Lord. He’s the one who can free your feet from traps you didn’t see coming.
verses.kjv: Mine eyes are ever toward the LORD; for he shall pluck my feet out of the net.

verses.text: What is man, that you think of him? What is the son of man, that you care for him? For you have made him a little lower than the angels, and crowned him with glory and honor.
verses.meaning: Next to the stars you might feel tiny, yet God keeps you in mind and has crowned you with honor.
verses.kjv: What is man, that thou art mindful of him? and the son of man, that thou visitest him? For thou hast made him a little lower than the angels, and hast crowned him with glory and honour.

verses.text: God said, “Behold, I have given you every herb yielding seed, which is on the surface of all the earth, and every tree, which bears fruit yielding seed. It will be your food.”
verses.meaning: From the very first page, God planned to feed you. The food on your plate began as his gift.
verses.kjv: And God said, Behold, I have given you every herb bearing seed, which is upon the face of all the earth, and every tree, in the which is the fruit of a tree yielding seed; to you it shall be for meat.

verses.text: Ruth said, “Don’t urge me to leave you, and to return from following you, for where you go, I will go; and where you stay, I will stay. Your people will be my people, and your God my God.”
verses.meaning: Ruth refused to leave her grieving mother-in-law. Loyal love sticks around when walking away is easier.
verses.kjv: And Ruth said, Intreat me not to leave thee, or to return from following after thee: for whither thou goest, I will go; and where thou lodgest, I will lodge: thy people shall be my people, and thy God my God…

verses.text: Mark the perfect man, and see the upright, for there is a future for the man of peace.
verses.meaning: Watch people who live honestly and well. A person of peace has a real future ahead.
verses.kjv: Mark the perfect man, and behold the upright: for the end of that man is peace.

verses.text: The LORD is my rock, my fortress, and my deliverer; my God, my rock, in whom I take refuge; my shield, and the horn of my salvation, my high tower.
verses.meaning: When you need somewhere safe, God is all of it: the solid ground, the walls, the shield and the rescue.
verses.kjv: The LORD is my rock, and my fortress, and my deliverer; my God, my strength, in whom I will trust; my buckler, and the horn of my salvation, and my high tower.

verses.text: For he has not despised nor abhorred the affliction of the afflicted, neither has he hidden his face from him; but when he cried to him, he heard.
verses.meaning: God doesn’t look away from people who are hurting. When they cry out to him, he listens.
verses.kjv: For he hath not despised nor abhorred the affliction of the afflicted; neither hath he hid his face from him; but when he cried unto him, he heard.

verses.text: She conceived again, and bore a son. She said, “This time I will praise the LORD.” Therefore she named him Judah. Then she stopped bearing.
verses.meaning: Leah had longed for her husband’s love. With her fourth son, she turned her focus to praising God instead.
verses.kjv: And she conceived again, and bare a son: and she said, Now will I praise the LORD: therefore she called his name Judah; and left bearing.

verses.text: Like a father has compassion on his children, so the LORD has compassion on those who fear him.
verses.meaning: God feels for you the way a good father feels for his child: tender, close and deeply caring.
verses.kjv: Like as a father pitieth his children, so the LORD pitieth them that fear him.

verses.text: Teach me to do your will, for you are my God. Your Spirit is good. Lead me in the land of uprightness.
verses.meaning: A prayer worth borrowing: ask God to teach you his will and let his good Spirit lead you on level ground.
verses.kjv: Teach me to do thy will; for thou art my God: thy spirit is good; lead me into the land of uprightness.

verses.text: He lay down and slept under a juniper tree; and behold, an angel touched him, and said to him, “Arise and eat!”
verses.meaning: When Elijah hit bottom, God’s first answer was sleep and a meal. Sometimes rest is the holy next step.
verses.kjv: And as he lay and slept under a juniper tree, behold, then an angel touched him, and said unto him, Arise and eat.

verses.text: He has swallowed up death forever! The Lord GOD will wipe away tears from off all faces. He will take the reproach of his people away from off all the earth, for the LORD has spoken it.
verses.meaning: One day God will swallow up death itself and gently wipe the tears from every face.
verses.kjv: He will swallow up death in victory; and the Lord GOD will wipe away tears from off all faces; and the rebuke of his people shall he take away from off all the earth: for the LORD hath spoken it.

verses.text: You have forgiven the iniquity of your people. You have covered all their sin. Selah.
verses.meaning: God doesn’t leave his people’s sin on display. He forgives it and covers every bit of it.
verses.kjv: Thou hast forgiven the iniquity of thy people, thou hast covered all their sin. Selah.

verses.text: Some trust in chariots, and some in horses, but we trust in the name of the LORD our God.
verses.meaning: Some people put their confidence in money, power or status. Put yours in God, who never fails.
verses.kjv: Some trust in chariots, and some in horses: but we will remember the name of the LORD our God.

verses.text: One thing I have asked of the LORD, that I will seek after: that I may dwell in the LORD’s house all the days of my life, to see the LORD’s beauty, and to inquire in his temple.
verses.meaning: David boiled his wants down to one: time near God, taking in his beauty. One clear desire steadies a life.
verses.kjv: One thing have I desired of the LORD, that will I seek after; that I may dwell in the house of the LORD all the days of my life, to behold the beauty of the LORD, and to enquire in his temple.

verses.text: Keep me as the apple of your eye. Hide me under the shadow of your wings…
verses.meaning: You can ask God to guard you as the most precious thing in his sight, sheltered close under his wings.
verses.kjv: Keep me as the apple of the eye, hide me under the shadow of thy wings…

verses.text: Abraham called the name of that place “The LORD Will Provide”. As it is said to this day, “On the LORD’s mountain, it will be provided.”
verses.meaning: Abraham named the mountain for what he learned there: God provides what you need right when it matters.
verses.kjv: And Abraham called the name of that place Jehovah-jireh: as it is said to this day, In the mount of the LORD it shall be seen.

verses.text: When he had finished speaking to Saul, the soul of Jonathan was knit with the soul of David, and Jonathan loved him as his own soul.
verses.meaning: Some friendships run soul deep, like Jonathan and David’s. A friend like that is one of life’s great gifts.
verses.kjv: And it came to pass, when he had made an end of speaking unto Saul, that the soul of Jonathan was knit with the soul of David, and Jonathan loved him as his own soul.

verses.text: I will hear what God, the LORD, will speak, for he will speak peace to his people, his saints; but let them not turn again to folly.
verses.meaning: Stop and listen for God: he speaks peace to his people, so don’t drift back into old foolishness.
verses.kjv: I will hear what God the LORD will speak: for he will speak peace unto his people, and to his saints: but let them not turn again to folly.

verses.text: A man’s steps are established by the LORD. He delights in his way. Though he stumble, he shall not fall, for the LORD holds him up with his hand.
verses.meaning: You may stumble, but you won’t be thrown down for good. God has hold of your hand the whole way.
verses.kjv: The steps of a good man are ordered by the LORD: and he delighteth in his way. Though he fall, he shall not be utterly cast down: for the LORD upholdeth him with his hand.

verses.text: Though I walk in the middle of trouble, you will revive me. You will stretch out your hand against the wrath of my enemies. Your right hand will save me.
verses.meaning: Even in the middle of trouble, God can breathe new life into you and keep you safe in his hand.
verses.kjv: Though I walk in the midst of trouble, thou wilt revive me: thou shalt stretch forth thine hand against the wrath of mine enemies, and thy right hand shall save me.

verses.text: I am not worthy of the least of all the loving kindnesses, and of all the truth, which you have shown to your servant; for with just my staff I crossed over this Jordan; and now I have become two companies.
verses.meaning: Jacob left with just a staff and came back with a whole household. He knew he hadn’t earned any of it.
verses.kjv: I am not worthy of the least of all the mercies, and of all the truth, which thou hast shewed unto thy servant; for with my staff I passed over this Jordan; and now I am become two bands.

verses.text: But the LORD’s loving kindness is from everlasting to everlasting with those who fear him, his righteousness to children’s children…
verses.meaning: God’s love had no beginning and has no end, and it reaches your children and their children too.
verses.kjv: But the mercy of the LORD is from everlasting to everlasting upon them that fear him, and his righteousness unto children’s children…

verses.text: Let the favor of the Lord our God be on us. Establish the work of our hands for us. Yes, establish the work of our hands.
verses.meaning: Ask God to bless your everyday work and make it last. Ordinary jobs matter when they’re placed in his hands.
verses.kjv: And let the beauty of the LORD our God be upon us: and establish thou the work of our hands upon us; yea, the work of our hands establish thou it.

verses.text: Stand in awe, and don’t sin. Search your own heart on your bed, and be still. Selah.
verses.meaning: Lying awake upset? Instead of stewing, search your heart before God and let yourself be still.
verses.kjv: Stand in awe, and sin not: commune with your own heart upon your bed, and be still. Selah.

verses.text: To provide for those who mourn in Zion, to give to them a garland for ashes, the oil of joy for mourning, the garment of praise for the spirit of heaviness, that they may be called trees of righteousness, the planting of the LORD, that he may be glorified.
verses.meaning: God trades ashes for a crown, mourning for joy and a heavy spirit for praise. Grief isn’t the end.
verses.kjv: To appoint unto them that mourn in Zion, to give unto them beauty for ashes, the oil of joy for mourning, the garment of praise for the spirit of heaviness; that they might be called trees of righteousness, the planting of the LORD, that he might be glorified.

verses.text: He has not dealt with us according to our sins, nor repaid us for our iniquities.
verses.meaning: Mercy, not payback: God doesn’t hand you what your wrongs have earned.
verses.kjv: He hath not dealt with us after our sins; nor rewarded us according to our iniquities.

verses.text: The wicked flee when no one pursues; but the righteous are as bold as a lion.
verses.meaning: A guilty conscience jumps at shadows. A heart that’s right with God can face things boldly, like a lion.
verses.kjv: The wicked flee when no man pursueth: but the righteous are bold as a lion.

verses.text: LORD, show me my end, what is the measure of my days. Let me know how frail I am.
verses.meaning: Asking God to show you how short life is isn’t gloomy. It helps you spend your days on what matters.
verses.kjv: LORD, make me to know mine end, and the measure of my days, what it is; that I may know how frail I am.

verses.text: He brought me out also into a large place. He delivered me, because he delighted in me.
verses.meaning: God didn’t rescue you out of duty. He brought you out into open space because he delights in you.
verses.kjv: He brought me forth also into a large place; he delivered me, because he delighted in me.

verses.text: He blessed Joseph, and said, “The God before whom my fathers Abraham and Isaac walked, the God who has fed me all my life long to this day…”
verses.meaning: Near the end of a messy, wandering life, Jacob could say that God had fed him every single day.
verses.kjv: And he blessed Joseph, and said, God, before whom my fathers Abraham and Isaac did walk, the God which fed me all my life long unto this day…

verses.text: Jonathan said to David, “Go in peace, because we have both sworn in the LORD’s name, saying, ‘The LORD is between me and you, and between my offspring and your offspring, forever.’” He arose and departed; and Jonathan went into the city.
verses.meaning: Jonathan and David put God at the center of their friendship, a bond that held even through goodbye.
verses.kjv: And Jonathan said to David, Go in peace, forasmuch as we have sworn both of us in the name of the LORD, saying, The LORD be between me and thee, and between my seed and thy seed for ever. And he arose and departed: and Jonathan went into the city.

verses.text: For my brothers’ and companions’ sakes, I will now say, “Peace be within you.”
verses.meaning: Wishing peace on others is one way to love them. Who could you pray peace over today?
verses.kjv: For my brethren and companions’ sakes, I will now say, Peace be within thee.

verses.text: Blessed are those whose strength is in you, who have set their hearts on a pilgrimage. Passing through the valley of Weeping, they make it a place of springs. Yes, the autumn rain covers it with blessings. They go from strength to strength. Every one of them appears before God in Zion.
verses.meaning: When your strength is in God, even a valley of tears can turn into a spring, and you keep growing stronger.
verses.kjv: Blessed is the man whose strength is in thee; in whose heart are the ways of them. Who passing through the valley of Baca make it a well; the rain also filleth the pools. They go from strength to strength, every one of them in Zion appeareth before God.

verses.text: Who among you fears the LORD and obeys the voice of his servant? He who walks in darkness and has no light, let him trust in the LORD’s name, and rely on his God.
verses.meaning: Walking in the dark with no light ahead? You can still lean on who God is and rely on him.
verses.kjv: Who is among you that feareth the LORD, that obeyeth the voice of his servant, that walketh in darkness, and hath no light? let him trust in the name of the LORD, and stay upon his God.

verses.text: You shall rejoice in all the good which the LORD your God has given to you, and to your house, you, and the Levite, and the foreigner who is among you.
verses.meaning: Enjoy the good things God has given your household, and invite others in. Shared joy is gratitude at its best.
verses.kjv: And thou shalt rejoice in every good thing which the LORD thy God hath given unto thee, and unto thine house, thou, and the Levite, and the stranger that is among you.

verses.text: I love the LORD, because he listens to my voice, and my cries for mercy.
verses.meaning: Love for God often grows from this: remembering that he heard you when you cried out.
verses.kjv: I love the LORD, because he hath heard my voice and my supplications.

verses.text: Yes, even when I am old and gray-haired, God, don’t forsake me, until I have declared your strength to the next generation, your might to everyone who is to come.
verses.meaning: Gray hair doesn’t end your purpose. There’s always someone younger who needs to hear what God has done.
verses.kjv: Now also when I am old and grayheaded, O God, forsake me not; until I have shewed thy strength unto this generation, and thy power to every one that is to come.

verses.text: Rest in the LORD, and wait patiently for him. Don’t fret because of him who prospers in his way, because of the man who makes wicked plots happen.
verses.meaning: Rest in God and wait for him. Others getting ahead by cheating doesn’t have to eat at you.
verses.kjv: Rest in the LORD, and wait patiently for him: fret not thyself because of him who prospereth in his way, because of the man who bringeth wicked devices to pass.

verses.text: For, behold, I create new heavens and a new earth; and the former things will not be remembered, nor come into mind.
verses.meaning: God is making everything new. The pain of the old world won’t even come to mind anymore.
verses.kjv: For, behold, I create new heavens and a new earth: and the former shall not be remembered, nor come into mind.

verses.text: If you, LORD, kept a record of sins, Lord, who could stand? But there is forgiveness with you, therefore you are feared.
verses.meaning: If God kept a tally of every wrong, no one would last. He forgives instead, and that draws you near in awe.
verses.kjv: If thou, LORD, shouldest mark iniquities, O Lord, who shall stand? But there is forgiveness with thee, that thou mayest be feared.

verses.text: Open your mouth for the mute, in the cause of all who are left desolate. Open your mouth, judge righteously, and serve justice to the poor and needy.
verses.meaning: Use your voice for people who can’t speak up for themselves. Courage often means standing up for the poor.
verses.kjv: Open thy mouth for the dumb in the cause of all such as are appointed to destruction. Open thy mouth, judge righteously, and plead the cause of the poor and needy.

verses.text: Teach me your way, LORD. I will walk in your truth. Make my heart undivided to fear your name.
verses.meaning: Divided attention makes a divided heart. Ask God to teach you his way and make your heart whole toward him.
verses.kjv: Teach me thy way, O LORD; I will walk in thy truth: unite my heart to fear thy name.

verses.text: When my father and my mother forsake me, then the LORD will take me up.
verses.meaning: Even if the people who should love you most walk away, God takes you in. You still have a home with him.
verses.kjv: When my father and my mother forsake me, then the LORD will take me up.

verses.text: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Behold, I will rain bread from the sky for you, and the people shall go out and gather a day’s portion every day, that I may test them, whether they will walk in my law or not.”
verses.meaning: God gave manna one day at a time, not a year in advance. Daily bread teaches you to trust him daily.
verses.kjv: Then said the LORD unto Moses, Behold, I will rain bread from heaven for you; and the people shall go out and gather a certain rate every day, that I may prove them, whether they will walk in my law, or no.

verses.text: David said to him, “Don’t be afraid, for I will surely show you kindness for Jonathan your father’s sake, and will restore to you all the land of Saul your father. You will eat bread at my table continually.”
verses.meaning: David honored his late friend Jonathan by caring for his disabled son and giving him a seat at the table.
verses.kjv: And David said unto him, Fear not: for I will surely shew thee kindness for Jonathan thy father’s sake, and will restore thee all the land of Saul thy father; and thou shalt eat bread at my table continually.

verses.text: My soul has had her dwelling too long with him who hates peace. I am for peace, but when I speak, they are for war.
verses.meaning: Sometimes you want peace and others want a fight. God hears that frustration, so bring it to him.
verses.kjv: My soul hath long dwelt with him that hateth peace. I am for peace: but when I speak, they are for war.

verses.text: My soul is weary with sorrow; strengthen me according to your word.
verses.meaning: Sorrow can wear you down. It’s okay to pray this honestly: lift me up, God, through what you’ve said.
verses.kjv: My soul melteth for heaviness: strengthen thou me according unto thy word.

verses.text: It will happen that before they call, I will answer; and while they are yet speaking, I will hear.
verses.meaning: God hears you before you finish praying. He’s listening even while you search for the words.
verses.kjv: And it shall come to pass, that before they call, I will answer; and while they are yet speaking, I will hear.

verses.text: The women said to Naomi, “Blessed be the LORD, who has not left you today without a near kinsman. Let his name be famous in Israel.”
verses.meaning: After years of loss, Naomi’s friends praised God for her new grandson. He hadn’t left her alone after all.
verses.kjv: And the women said unto Naomi, Blessed be the LORD, which hath not left thee this day without a kinsman, that his name may be famous in Israel.

verses.text: Cause me to hear your loving kindness in the morning, for I trust in you. Cause me to know the way in which I should walk, for I lift up my soul to you.
verses.meaning: Start your day listening for God’s love, then ask him to show you which way to walk.
verses.kjv: Cause me to hear thy lovingkindness in the morning; for in thee do I trust: cause me to know the way wherein I should walk; for I lift up my soul unto thee.

verses.text: Not to us, LORD, not to us, but to your name give glory, for your loving kindness, and for your truth’s sake.
verses.meaning: The goal isn’t to make your own name big. Point the credit to God, whose love and faithfulness deserve it.
verses.kjv: Not unto us, O LORD, not unto us, but unto thy name give glory, for thy mercy, and for thy truth’s sake.

verses.text: I said, “Oh that I had wings like a dove! Then I would fly away, and be at rest.”
verses.meaning: Ever wanted to fly away from it all? David did too. You can bring that tired longing honestly to God.
verses.kjv: And I said, Oh that I had wings like a dove! for then would I fly away, and be at rest.

verses.text: Then the LORD’s ransomed ones will return, and come with singing to Zion; and everlasting joy will be on their heads. They will obtain gladness and joy, and sorrow and sighing will flee away.
verses.meaning: A day is coming when God’s people come home singing, and sorrow and sighing run away for good.
verses.kjv: And the ransomed of the LORD shall return, and come to Zion with songs and everlasting joy upon their heads: they shall obtain joy and gladness, and sorrow and sighing shall flee away.

verses.text: Don’t say, “I will pay back evil.” Wait for the LORD, and he will save you.
verses.meaning: When you want to get even, wait on God instead. Payback isn’t yours to carry; he will rescue you.
verses.kjv: Say not thou, I will recompense evil; but wait on the LORD, and he shall save thee.

verses.text: Listen to me, you who know righteousness, the people in whose heart is my law. Don’t fear the reproach of men, and don’t be dismayed at their insults.
verses.meaning: When people mock you for living God’s way, don’t let it scare you. Their insults fade; God’s goodness lasts.
verses.kjv: Hearken unto me, ye that know righteousness, the people in whose heart is my law; fear ye not the reproach of men, neither be ye afraid of their revilings.

verses.text: I will set no vile thing before my eyes. I hate the deeds of faithless men. They will not cling to me.
verses.meaning: David refused to put anything worthless in front of his eyes. You get to choose what fills your screen too.
verses.kjv: I will set no wicked thing before mine eyes: I hate the work of them that turn aside; it shall not cleave to me.

verses.text: They looked to him, and were radiant. Their faces shall never be covered with shame.
verses.meaning: Look to God and your face lights up. Shame doesn’t get the last word on who you are.
verses.kjv: They looked unto him, and were lightened: and their faces were not ashamed.

verses.text: When they measured it with an omer, he who gathered much had nothing over, and he who gathered little had no lack. They each gathered according to his eating.
verses.meaning: With manna, nobody had too much and nobody went short. God measures what he gives to what you need.
verses.kjv: And when they did mete it with an omer, he that gathered much had nothing over, and he that gathered little had no lack; they gathered every man according to his eating.

verses.text: So they sat down with him on the ground seven days and seven nights, and no one spoke a word to him, for they saw that his grief was very great.
verses.meaning: Before saying anything, Job’s friends sat with him in silence for a week. Sometimes presence is enough.
verses.kjv: So they sat down with him upon the ground seven days and seven nights, and none spake a word unto him: for they saw that his grief was very great.

verses.text: He makes wars cease to the end of the earth. He breaks the bow, and shatters the spear. He burns the chariots in the fire.
verses.meaning: God is able to end wars, snapping weapons like sticks. No conflict is bigger than he is.
verses.kjv: He maketh wars to cease unto the end of the earth; he breaketh the bow, and cutteth the spear in sunder; he burneth the chariot in the fire.

verses.text: In the day that I called, you answered me. You encouraged me with strength in my soul.
verses.meaning: God answers when you call, and one of his answers is fresh courage and strength deep inside you.
verses.kjv: In the day when I cried thou answeredst me, and strengthenedst me with strength in my soul.

verses.text: I will bring the blind by a way that they don’t know. I will lead them in paths that they don’t know. I will make darkness light before them, and crooked places straight. I will do these things, and I will not forsake them.
verses.meaning: You don’t need to see the whole road. God leads people down unfamiliar paths and lights up the dark.
verses.kjv: And I will bring the blind by a way that they knew not; I will lead them in paths that they have not known: I will make darkness light before them, and crooked things straight. These things will I do unto them, and not forsake them.

verses.text: Then Samuel took a stone and set it between Mizpah and Shen, and called its name Ebenezer, saying, “The LORD helped us until now.”
verses.meaning: Samuel set up a stone to remember God’s help. Mark the moments God came through so you don’t forget them.
verses.kjv: Then Samuel took a stone, and set it between Mizpeh and Shen, and called the name of it Eben-ezer, saying, Hitherto hath the LORD helped us.

verses.text: The LORD takes pleasure in those who fear him, in those who hope in his loving kindness.
verses.meaning: God isn’t impressed by raw strength. He delights in people who put their hope in his love.
verses.kjv: The LORD taketh pleasure in them that fear him, in those that hope in his mercy.

verses.text: Serve the LORD with gladness. Come before his presence with singing.
verses.meaning: Serving God isn’t meant to be grim duty. Bring gladness to it, and come close to him with a song.
verses.kjv: Serve the LORD with gladness: come before his presence with singing.

verses.text: He who dwells in the secret place of the Most High will rest in the shadow of the Almighty.
verses.meaning: Staying close to God is like resting in the shade of the Almighty. You’re covered there.
verses.kjv: He that dwelleth in the secret place of the most High shall abide under the shadow of the Almighty.

verses.text: Therefore the LORD will wait, that he may be gracious to you; and therefore he will be exalted, that he may have mercy on you, for the LORD is a God of justice. Blessed are all those who wait for him.
verses.meaning: Even after his people turned away, God waited to be kind to them. He’s waiting to show you mercy too.
verses.kjv: And therefore will the LORD wait, that he may be gracious unto you, and therefore will he be exalted, that he may have mercy upon you: for the LORD is a God of judgment: blessed are all they that wait for him.

verses.text: He touched my mouth with it, and said, “Behold, this has touched your lips; and your iniquity is taken away, and your sin forgiven.”
verses.meaning: Isaiah felt undone by his own sin. Then God stepped in, took the guilt away and made him ready to serve.
verses.kjv: And he laid it upon my mouth, and said, Lo, this hath touched thy lips; and thine iniquity is taken away, and thy sin purged.

verses.text: But the LORD said to me, “Don’t say, ‘I am a child;’ for you must go to whomever I send you, and you must say whatever I command you. Don’t be afraid because of them, for I am with you to rescue you,” says the LORD.
verses.meaning: Jeremiah felt too young. God said age wasn’t the issue: go where I send you, and I’ll be with you.
verses.kjv: But the LORD said unto me, Say not, I am a child: for thou shalt go to all that I shall send thee, and whatsoever I command thee thou shalt speak. Be not afraid of their faces: for I am with thee to deliver thee, saith the LORD.
