verses.text: How can a young man keep his way pure? By living according to your word. With my whole heart I have sought you. Don’t let me wander from your commandments. I have hidden your word in my heart, that I might not sin against you.
verses.meaning: Staying pure starts with God’s word stored inside you, so it’s already there when temptation shows up.
verses.kjv: Wherewithal shall a young man cleanse his way? by taking heed thereto according to thy word. With my whole heart have I sought thee: O let me not wander from thy commandments. Thy word have I hid in mine heart, that I might not sin against thee.

verses.text: You know my sitting down and my rising up. You perceive my thoughts from afar. You search out my path and my lying down, and are acquainted with all my ways.
verses.meaning: God notices when you sit down and when you get up. He knows every path you take, inside and out.
verses.kjv: Thou knowest my downsitting and mine uprising, thou understandest my thought afar off. Thou compassest my path and my lying down, and art acquainted with all my ways.

verses.text: You shall not glean your vineyard, neither shall you gather the fallen grapes of your vineyard. You shall leave them for the poor and for the foreigner. I am the LORD your God.
verses.meaning: God built kindness into every harvest: leave some for the poor. Part of what you have is meant for others.
verses.kjv: And thou shalt not glean thy vineyard, neither shalt thou gather every grape of thy vineyard; thou shalt leave them for the poor and stranger: I am the LORD your God.

verses.text: Oh magnify the LORD with me. Let’s exalt his name together.
verses.meaning: Praise gets louder together. Invite someone to celebrate God’s goodness with you.
verses.kjv: O magnify the LORD with me, and let us exalt his name together.

verses.text: He makes the storm a calm, so that its waves are still. Then they are glad because it is calm, so he brings them to their desired haven.
verses.meaning: God can hush a storm to stillness and bring frightened people safely to the harbor they longed for.
verses.kjv: He maketh the storm a calm, so that the waves thereof are still. Then are they glad because they be quiet; so he bringeth them unto their desired haven.

verses.text: You therefore must endure hardship as a good soldier of Christ Jesus.
verses.meaning: Following Jesus includes hard days. Like a committed soldier, you can take the hits and stay at your post.
verses.kjv: Thou therefore endure hardness, as a good soldier of Jesus Christ.

verses.text: I chattered like a swallow or a crane. I moaned like a dove. My eyes weaken looking upward. Lord, I am oppressed. Be my security.
verses.meaning: Sick and scared, King Hezekiah could only moan and look up: Lord, be my security. That still counts as prayer.
verses.kjv: Like a crane or a swallow, so did I chatter: I did mourn as a dove: mine eyes fail with looking upward: O LORD, I am oppressed; undertake for me.

verses.text: Then David the king went in and sat before the LORD; and he said, “Who am I, Lord GOD, and what is my house, that you have brought me this far?”
verses.meaning: A shepherd boy turned king sat amazed before God. Gratitude begins with wonder at how far you’ve come.
verses.kjv: Then went king David in, and sat before the LORD, and he said, Who am I, O Lord GOD? and what is my house, that thou hast brought me hitherto?

verses.text: For whom the LORD loves, he corrects, even as a father reproves the son in whom he delights.
verses.meaning: God’s correction isn’t rejection. Like a loving parent, he guides you because he delights in you.
verses.kjv: For whom the LORD loveth he correcteth; even as a father the son in whom he delighteth.

verses.text: I declare the end from the beginning, and from ancient times things that are not yet done. I say: My counsel will stand, and I will do all that I please.
verses.meaning: God sees the end from the beginning, and his purposes always stand. You can trust the one writing the story.
verses.kjv: Declaring the end from the beginning, and from ancient times the things that are not yet done, saying, My counsel shall stand, and I will do all my pleasure…

verses.text: Return to your rest, my soul, for the LORD has dealt bountifully with you.
verses.meaning: Tell your restless soul to settle down: look how good God has already been to you.
verses.kjv: Return unto thy rest, O my soul; for the LORD hath dealt bountifully with thee.

verses.text: Sing, heavens, and be joyful, earth! Break out into singing, mountains! For the LORD has comforted his people, and will have compassion on his afflicted.
verses.meaning: Heaven and earth are told to sing, because God comforts his people and has compassion on the hurting.
verses.kjv: Sing, O heavens; and be joyful, O earth; and break forth into singing, O mountains: for the LORD hath comforted his people, and will have mercy upon his afflicted.

verses.text: Behold, for peace I had great anguish, but you have in love for my soul delivered it from the pit of corruption; for you have cast all my sins behind your back.
verses.meaning: Hezekiah thanked God for pulling him back from the edge of death and tossing every sin out of sight.
verses.kjv: Behold, for peace I had great bitterness: but thou hast in love to my soul delivered it from the pit of corruption: for thou hast cast all my sins behind thy back.

verses.text: You, son of man, don’t be afraid of them, neither be afraid of their words, though briers and thorns are with you, and you dwell among scorpions. Don’t be afraid of their words, nor be dismayed at their looks, though they are a rebellious house.
verses.meaning: God sent Ezekiel to hostile people and told him not to fear their words or their glares. Speak truth anyway.
verses.kjv: And thou, son of man, be not afraid of them, neither be afraid of their words, though briers and thorns be with thee, and thou dost dwell among scorpions: be not afraid of their words, nor be dismayed at their looks, though they be a rebellious house.

verses.text: Open my eyes, that I may see wondrous things out of your law.
verses.meaning: Ask God to open your eyes before you open the Bible. There are wonders in it you’ll only see with his help.
verses.kjv: Open thou mine eyes, that I may behold wondrous things out of thy law.

verses.text: How precious to me are your thoughts, God! How vast is their sum!
verses.meaning: David marveled at how precious and countless God’s thoughts are. You’re never far from his mind.
verses.kjv: How precious also are thy thoughts unto me, O God! how great is the sum of them!

verses.text: For the LORD your God has blessed you in all the work of your hands. He has known your walking through this great wilderness. These forty years, the LORD your God has been with you. You have lacked nothing.
verses.meaning: Forty years in a desert, and God’s people never went without. He knows every step of your wilderness too.
verses.kjv: For the LORD thy God hath blessed thee in all the works of thy hand: he knoweth thy walking through this great wilderness: these forty years the LORD thy God hath been with thee; thou hast lacked nothing.

verses.text: God sets the lonely in families. He brings out the prisoners with singing, but the rebellious dwell in a sun-scorched land.
verses.meaning: God cares about loneliness. He brings isolated people into families and places where they belong.
verses.kjv: God setteth the solitary in families: he bringeth out those which are bound with chains: but the rebellious dwell in a dry land.

verses.text: Her ways are ways of pleasantness. All her paths are peace.
verses.meaning: Wisdom’s path isn’t grim. Walking God’s wise way leads to a pleasant, peaceful life.
verses.kjv: Her ways are ways of pleasantness, and all her paths are peace.

verses.text: For consider him who has endured such contradiction of sinners against himself, that you don’t grow weary, fainting in your souls.
verses.meaning: When you’re ready to quit, think about all that Jesus endured for you. It puts fresh fight back in your soul.
verses.kjv: For consider him that endured such contradiction of sinners against himself, lest ye be wearied and faint in your minds.

verses.text: Surely he has borne our sickness and carried our suffering; yet we considered him plagued, struck by God, and afflicted.
verses.meaning: The pain and sorrow you carry, Jesus carried too. He isn’t distant from your suffering.
verses.kjv: Surely he hath borne our griefs, and carried our sorrows: yet we did esteem him stricken, smitten of God, and afflicted.

verses.text: Blessed be the LORD, who has given rest to his people Israel, according to all that he promised. There has not failed one word of all his good promise, which he promised by Moses his servant.
verses.meaning: At the temple’s dedication, Solomon praised God for keeping every single promise. Not one had fallen short.
verses.kjv: Blessed be the LORD, that hath given rest unto his people Israel, according to all that he promised: there hath not failed one word of all his good promise, which he promised by the hand of Moses his servant.

verses.text: Better is a dinner of herbs, where love is, than a fattened calf with hatred.
verses.meaning: A simple meal with people who love each other beats a feast where there’s tension and contempt.
verses.kjv: Better is a dinner of herbs where love is, than a stalled ox and hatred therewith.

verses.text: I delight to do your will, my God. Yes, your law is within my heart.
verses.meaning: Doing God’s will can become a delight, not a chore, when his words live deep in your heart.
verses.kjv: I delight to do thy will, O my God: yea, thy law is within my heart.

verses.text: Yes, the sparrow has found a home, and the swallow a nest for herself, where she may have her young, near your altars, LORD of Armies, my King, and my God.
verses.meaning: Sparrows and swallows found a home near God’s altar. There’s a place for you to settle near him too.
verses.kjv: Yea, the sparrow hath found an house, and the swallow a nest for herself, where she may lay her young, even thine altars, O LORD of hosts, my King, and my God.

verses.text: Your sun will not go down any more, nor will your moon withdraw itself; for the LORD will be your everlasting light, and the days of your mourning will end.
verses.meaning: God promises a day when he himself is a light that never sets, and your days of mourning are over.
verses.kjv: Thy sun shall no more go down; neither shall thy moon withdraw itself: for the LORD shall be thine everlasting light, and the days of thy mourning shall be ended.

verses.text: All we like sheep have gone astray. Everyone has turned to his own way; and the LORD has laid on him the iniquity of us all.
verses.meaning: All of us have wandered off like lost sheep, and God laid the weight of all that wandering on Jesus.
verses.kjv: All we like sheep have gone astray; we have turned every one to his own way; and the LORD hath laid on him the iniquity of us all.

verses.text: If it happens, our God whom we serve is able to deliver us from the burning fiery furnace; and he will deliver us out of your hand, O king. But if not, let it be known to you, O king, that we will not serve your gods or worship the golden image which you have set up.
verses.meaning: Three friends knew God could save them from the fire, and they stayed loyal to him whether he did or not.
verses.kjv: If it be so, our God whom we serve is able to deliver us from the burning fiery furnace, and he will deliver us out of thine hand, O king. But if not, be it known unto thee, O king, that we will not serve thy gods, nor worship the golden image which thou hast set up.

verses.text: Turn my heart toward your statutes, not toward selfish gain.
verses.meaning: Pray for a heart that leans toward God’s ways instead of always chasing more for yourself.
verses.kjv: Incline my heart unto thy testimonies, and not to covetousness.

verses.text: For the LORD takes pleasure in his people. He crowns the humble with salvation.
verses.meaning: God enjoys his people, and he puts a crown of rescue on the humble, not on the impressive.
verses.kjv: For the LORD taketh pleasure in his people: he will beautify the meek with salvation.

verses.text: He executes justice for the fatherless and widow and loves the foreigner in giving him food and clothing.
verses.meaning: God stands up for orphans and widows and gives outsiders food and clothes. No one is beneath his notice.
verses.kjv: He doth execute the judgment of the fatherless and widow, and loveth the stranger, in giving him food and raiment.

verses.text: “Defend the weak, the poor, and the fatherless. Maintain the rights of the poor and oppressed. Rescue the weak and needy. Deliver them out of the hand of the wicked.”
verses.meaning: Stand up for the weak, the poor and the orphan. Protecting vulnerable people is God’s work for you too.
verses.kjv: Defend the poor and fatherless: do justice to the afflicted and needy. Deliver the poor and needy: rid them out of the hand of the wicked.

verses.text: Deceit is in the heart of those who plot evil, but joy comes to the promoters of peace.
verses.meaning: Scheming eats away at you, but working for peace brings a joy that lasts.
verses.kjv: Deceit is in the heart of them that imagine evil: but to the counsellors of peace is joy.

verses.text: For you need endurance so that, having done the will of God, you may receive the promise.
verses.meaning: Doing God’s will often takes staying power. Keep at it: what he has promised is worth the wait.
verses.kjv: For ye have need of patience, that, after ye have done the will of God, ye might receive the promise.

verses.text: Then he said to me, “Don’t be afraid, Daniel; for from the first day that you set your heart to understand, and to humble yourself before your God, your words were heard. I have come for your words’ sake.”
verses.meaning: Daniel’s prayer was heard the very first day he prayed. Yours are heard too, before you see any answer.
verses.kjv: Then said he unto me, Fear not, Daniel: for from the first day that thou didst set thine heart to understand, and to chasten thyself before thy God, thy words were heard, and I am come for thy words.

verses.text: But who am I, and what is my people, that we should be able to offer so willingly as this? For all things come from you, and we have given you of your own.
verses.meaning: Anything you give God was his gift to you first. Giving is simply handing back what he placed in your hands.
verses.kjv: But who am I, and what is my people, that we should be able to offer so willingly after this sort? for all things come of thee, and of thine own have we given thee.

verses.text: Many waters can’t quench love, neither can floods drown it. If a man would give all the wealth of his house for love, he would be utterly scorned.
verses.meaning: Real love can’t be drowned by floods or bought with money. It’s a gift, not a transaction.
verses.kjv: Many waters cannot quench love, neither can the floods drown it: if a man would give all the substance of his house for love, it would utterly be contemned.

verses.text: He who follows after righteousness and kindness finds life, righteousness, and honor.
verses.meaning: Chase goodness and kindness, and you’ll find a full, meaningful life waiting along that road.
verses.kjv: He that followeth after righteousness and mercy findeth life, righteousness, and honour.

verses.text: When you walk, it will lead you. When you sleep, it will watch over you. When you awake, it will talk with you.
verses.meaning: Wisdom you take to heart goes with you: guiding your steps, guarding your sleep, speaking when you wake.
verses.kjv: When thou goest, it shall lead thee; when thou sleepest, it shall keep thee; and when thou awakest, it shall talk with thee.

verses.text: “There is hope for your latter end,” says the LORD. “Your children will come again to their own territory.”
verses.meaning: Spoken to a weeping mother: your story isn’t over. There is still hope for what lies ahead.
verses.kjv: And there is hope in thine end, saith the LORD, that thy children shall come again to their own border.

verses.text: Let the wicked forsake his way, and the unrighteous man his thoughts. Let him return to the LORD, and he will have mercy on him, to our God, for he will freely pardon.
verses.meaning: It’s never too late to turn around. Come back to God and you’ll find a generous, full pardon waiting.
verses.kjv: Let the wicked forsake his way, and the unrighteous man his thoughts: and let him return unto the LORD, and he will have mercy upon him; and to our God, for he will abundantly pardon.

verses.text: It shall come to pass that, as you were a curse among the nations, house of Judah and house of Israel, so I will save you, and you shall be a blessing. Don’t be afraid. Let your hands be strong.
verses.meaning: God promised to turn his people’s shame into blessing. So don’t be afraid; let your hands get busy.
verses.kjv: And it shall come to pass, that as ye were a curse among the heathen, O house of Judah, and house of Israel; so will I save you, and ye shall be a blessing: fear not, but let your hands be strong.

verses.text: Set a watch, LORD, before my mouth. Keep the door of my lips.
verses.meaning: Picture God posting a guard at the door of your lips. Some words, and some comments, are better left unsaid.
verses.kjv: Set a watch, O LORD, before my mouth; keep the door of my lips.

verses.text: You whom I have taken hold of from the ends of the earth, and called from its corners, and said to you, ‘You are my servant. I have chosen you and have not cast you away.’
verses.meaning: God went to the ends of the earth for you. He chose you, and he hasn’t thrown you away.
verses.kjv: Thou whom I have taken from the ends of the earth, and called thee from the chief men thereof, and said unto thee, Thou art my servant; I have chosen thee, and not cast thee away.

verses.text: Then she arose with her daughters-in-law, that she might return from the country of Moab; for she had heard in the country of Moab how the LORD had visited his people in giving them bread.
verses.meaning: Naomi heard that God had given her people bread again, and that news is what brought her home.
verses.kjv: Then she arose with her daughters in law, that she might return from the country of Moab: for she had heard in the country of Moab how that the LORD had visited his people in giving them bread.

verses.text: One generation will commend your works to another, and will declare your mighty acts.
verses.meaning: Tell the younger people in your life what God has done. Faith travels through shared stories.
verses.kjv: One generation shall praise thy works to another, and shall declare thy mighty acts.

verses.text: When a man’s ways please the LORD, he makes even his enemies to be at peace with him.
verses.meaning: Living to please God can soften even hostile people. Peace with others often starts there.
verses.kjv: When a man’s ways please the LORD, he maketh even his enemies to be at peace with him.

verses.text: Therefore lift up the hands that hang down and the feeble knees, and make straight paths for your feet, so what is lame may not be dislocated, but rather be healed.
verses.meaning: Tired arms and shaky knees? Get up and keep walking a straight path, so what’s weak in you can heal.
verses.kjv: Wherefore lift up the hands which hang down, and the feeble knees; And make straight paths for your feet, lest that which is lame be turned out of the way; but let it rather be healed.

verses.text: When my soul fainted within me, I remembered the LORD. My prayer came in to you, into your holy temple.
verses.meaning: At his lowest point, Jonah remembered God and prayed. Even a faint, worn out prayer reaches him.
verses.kjv: When my soul fainted within me I remembered the LORD: and my prayer came in unto thee, into thine holy temple.

verses.text: They sang to one another in praising and giving thanks to the LORD, “For he is good, for his loving kindness endures forever toward Israel.” All the people shouted with a great shout, when they praised the LORD, because the foundation of the LORD’s house had been laid.
verses.meaning: The exiles shouted thanks over a bare foundation. Thank God for new beginnings, not only finished work.
verses.kjv: And they sang together by course in praising and giving thanks unto the LORD; because he is good, for his mercy endureth for ever toward Israel. And all the people shouted with a great shout, when they praised the LORD, because the foundation of the house of the LORD was laid.

verses.text: “In overflowing wrath I hid my face from you for a moment, but with everlasting loving kindness I will have mercy on you,” says the LORD your Redeemer.
verses.meaning: God’s anger lasts a moment, but his kindness lasts forever. Mercy is his final word to his people.
verses.kjv: In a little wrath I hid my face from thee for a moment; but with everlasting kindness will I have mercy on thee, saith the LORD thy Redeemer.

verses.text: This is the end of the matter. All has been heard. Fear God and keep his commandments; for this is the whole duty of man.
verses.meaning: After weighing everything, the Teacher boiled life down: honor God and do what he says. That’s the point.
verses.kjv: Let us hear the conclusion of the whole matter: Fear God, and keep his commandments: for this is the whole duty of man.

verses.text: Don’t weary yourself to be rich. In your wisdom, show restraint.
verses.meaning: Don’t wear yourself out chasing more money. Wisdom knows when to stop.
verses.kjv: Labour not to be rich: cease from thine own wisdom.

verses.text: Behold, I am the LORD, the God of all flesh. Is there anything too hard for me?
verses.meaning: God asks a question worth holding on to: is anything too hard for me? Nothing is beyond him.
verses.kjv: Behold, I am the LORD, the God of all flesh: is there any thing too hard for me?

verses.text: Return, you backsliding children, and I will heal your backsliding. “Behold, we have come to you; for you are the LORD our God.”
verses.meaning: God calls wandering people home and promises to heal their habit of drifting. You can always come back.
verses.kjv: Return, ye backsliding children, and I will heal your backslidings. Behold, we come unto thee; for thou art the LORD our God.

verses.text: For I am not ashamed of the Good News of Christ, because it is the power of God for salvation for everyone who believes, for the Jew first, and also for the Greek.
verses.meaning: Paul wasn’t embarrassed by the good news of Jesus. It carries God’s power to save anyone who trusts him.
verses.kjv: For I am not ashamed of the gospel of Christ: for it is the power of God unto salvation to every one that believeth; to the Jew first, and also to the Greek.

verses.text: Don’t turn to the right hand nor to the left. Remove your foot from evil.
verses.meaning: Stay on the path without drifting left or right, and step away from whatever pulls you toward wrong.
verses.kjv: Turn not to the right hand nor to the left: remove thy foot from evil.

verses.text: This is what the LORD who made you, and formed you from the womb, who will help you says: “Don’t be afraid, Jacob my servant; and you, Jeshurun, whom I have chosen.”
verses.meaning: The God who shaped you before birth promises to help you. You’re chosen, so you don’t have to fear.
verses.kjv: Thus saith the LORD that made thee, and formed thee from the womb, which will help thee; Fear not, O Jacob, my servant; and thou, Jesurun, whom I have chosen.

verses.text: The ravens brought him bread and meat in the morning, and bread and meat in the evening; and he drank from the brook.
verses.meaning: God fed Elijah through ravens, morning and evening. He can use the most unlikely helpers to care for you.
verses.kjv: And the ravens brought him bread and flesh in the morning, and bread and flesh in the evening; and he drank of the brook.

verses.text: Don’t withhold good from those to whom it is due, when it is in the power of your hand to do it. Don’t say to your neighbor, “Go, and come again; tomorrow I will give it to you,” when you have it by you.
verses.meaning: If you can help someone today, don’t make them wait until tomorrow. Do the good that’s in your hands.
verses.kjv: Withhold not good from them to whom it is due, when it is in the power of thine hand to do it. Say not unto thy neighbour, Go, and come again, and to morrow I will give; when thou hast it by thee.

verses.text: The beginning of strife is like breaching a dam, therefore stop contention before quarreling breaks out.
verses.meaning: A quarrel is like a crack in a dam: easy to stop early, impossible once it bursts. Drop it early.
verses.kjv: The beginning of strife is as when one letteth out water: therefore leave off contention, before it be meddled with.

verses.text: If anyone speaks, let it be as it were the very words of God. If anyone serves, let it be as of the strength which God supplies, that in all things God may be glorified through Jesus Christ, to whom belong the glory and the dominion forever and ever. Amen.
verses.meaning: Whatever way you serve, run on the strength God supplies, not your own, so he gets the credit.
verses.kjv: If any man speak, let him speak as the oracles of God; if any man minister, let him do it as of the ability which God giveth: that God in all things may be glorified through Jesus Christ, to whom be praise and dominion for ever and ever. Amen.

verses.text: I called on your name, LORD, out of the lowest dungeon. You heard my voice: “Don’t hide your ear from my sighing, and my cry.”
verses.meaning: From the deepest pit, the writer called out and God heard. Your sighs count as prayers too.
verses.kjv: I called upon thy name, O LORD, out of the low dungeon. Thou hast heard my voice: hide not thine ear at my breathing, at my cry.

verses.text: He said, “Naked I came out of my mother’s womb, and naked will I return there. The LORD gave, and the LORD has taken away. Blessed be the LORD’s name.”
verses.meaning: Even in crushing loss, Job blessed God. Everything you hold is a gift, and the Giver is still worth praising.
verses.kjv: And said, Naked came I out of my mother’s womb, and naked shall I return thither: the LORD gave, and the LORD hath taken away; blessed be the name of the LORD.

verses.text: In all their affliction he was afflicted, and the angel of his presence saved them. In his love and in his pity he redeemed them. He bore them, and carried them all the days of old.
verses.meaning: God doesn’t watch your suffering from far away. He feels it with you and carries you in his love.
verses.kjv: In all their affliction he was afflicted, and the angel of his presence saved them: in his love and in his pity he redeemed them; and he bare them, and carried them all the days of old.

verses.text: In the morning sow your seed, and in the evening don’t withhold your hand; for you don’t know which will prosper, whether this or that, or whether they both will be equally good.
verses.meaning: Nobody knows which efforts will bear fruit, so keep sowing morning and evening. Leave the results to God.
verses.kjv: In the morning sow thy seed, and in the evening withhold not thine hand: for thou knowest not whether shall prosper, either this or that, or whether they both shall be alike good.

verses.text: The sleep of a laboring man is sweet, whether he eats little or much; but the abundance of the rich will not allow him to sleep.
verses.meaning: Honest work brings sweet sleep, while always wanting more can keep you awake at night.
verses.kjv: The sleep of a labouring man is sweet, whether he eat little or much: but the abundance of the rich will not suffer him to sleep.

verses.text: For the Lord will not cast off forever. For though he causes grief, yet he will have compassion according to the multitude of his loving kindnesses.
verses.meaning: Hard seasons don’t last forever. God’s compassion and steady love always outlast the grief.
verses.kjv: For the Lord will not cast off for ever: But though he cause grief, yet will he have compassion according to the multitude of his mercies.

verses.text: “They will no longer each teach his neighbor, and every man teach his brother, saying, ‘Know the LORD;’ for they will all know me, from their least to their greatest,” says the LORD, “for I will forgive their iniquity, and I will remember their sin no more.”
verses.meaning: God’s new promise: he forgives your wrongs and chooses never to bring them up again.
verses.kjv: And they shall teach no more every man his neighbour, and every man his brother, saying, Know the LORD: for they shall all know me, from the least of them unto the greatest of them, saith the LORD: for I will forgive their iniquity, and I will remember their sin no more.

verses.text: Peter answered him and said, “Lord, if it is you, command me to come to you on the waters.” He said, “Come!” Peter stepped down from the boat and walked on the waters to come to Jesus.
verses.meaning: Peter asked, Jesus said come, and Peter stepped out onto the water. Faith sometimes means leaving the boat.
verses.kjv: And Peter answered him and said, Lord, if it be thou, bid me come unto thee on the water. And he said, Come. And when Peter was come down out of the ship, he walked on the water, to go to Jesus.

verses.text: Go to the ant, you sluggard. Consider her ways, and be wise; which having no chief, overseer, or ruler, provides her bread in the summer, and gathers her food in the harvest.
verses.meaning: Nobody has to boss the ant around; it works while the season is right. Use the time you have today wisely.
verses.kjv: Go to the ant, thou sluggard; consider her ways, and be wise: Which having no guide, overseer, or ruler, Provideth her meat in the summer, and gathereth her food in the harvest.

verses.text: Listen to me, house of Jacob, and all the remnant of the house of Israel, that have been carried from their birth, that have been carried from the womb.
verses.meaning: Since before your first breath, God has been carrying his people. You’ve been held longer than you know.
verses.kjv: Hearken unto me, O house of Jacob, and all the remnant of the house of Israel, which are borne by me from the belly, which are carried from the womb…

verses.text: The jar of meal didn’t run out and the jar of oil didn’t fail, according to the LORD’s word, which he spoke by Elijah.
verses.meaning: A widow shared her last flour with a stranger, and God kept her jar from running dry, one day at a time.
verses.kjv: And the barrel of meal wasted not, neither did the cruse of oil fail, according to the word of the LORD, which he spake by Elijah.

verses.text: One who walks with wise men grows wise, but a companion of fools suffers harm.
verses.meaning: You become like the people you spend time with. Choose friends who make you wiser.
verses.kjv: He that walketh with wise men shall be wise: but a companion of fools shall be destroyed.

verses.text: It is an honor for a man to keep aloof from strife, but every fool will be quarreling.
verses.meaning: Walking away from a pointless fight isn’t weakness. It’s honorable; anyone can pick a quarrel.
verses.kjv: It is an honour for a man to cease from strife: but every fool will be meddling.

verses.text: I have written to you, fathers, because you know him who is from the beginning. I have written to you, young men, because you are strong, and the word of God remains in you, and you have overcome the evil one.
verses.meaning: Real strength comes from God’s word living in you. It’s what helps you stand your ground against evil.
verses.kjv: I have written unto you, fathers, because ye have known him that is from the beginning. I have written unto you, young men, because ye are strong, and the word of God abideth in you, and ye have overcome the wicked one.

verses.text: Behold, I am with you, and will keep you, wherever you go, and will bring you again into this land. For I will not leave you until I have done that which I have spoken of to you.
verses.meaning: God promised Jacob, alone and on the run: I’m with you wherever you go, and I won’t leave you.
verses.kjv: And, behold, I am with thee, and will keep thee in all places whither thou goest, and will bring thee again into this land; for I will not leave thee, until I have done that which I have spoken to thee of.

verses.text: I thank you and praise you, O God of my fathers, who have given me wisdom and might, and have now made known to me what we desired of you; for you have made known to us the king’s matter.
verses.meaning: When God answered his urgent prayer, Daniel stopped first to thank him. Don’t rush past your answered prayers.
verses.kjv: I thank thee, and praise thee, O thou God of my fathers, who hast given me wisdom and might, and hast made known unto me now what we desired of thee: for thou hast now made known unto us the king’s matter.

verses.text: I will betroth you to me forever. Yes, I will betroth you to me in righteousness, in justice, in loving kindness, and in compassion.
verses.meaning: God commits to his people like a faithful groom: forever, with fairness, kindness and tender compassion.
verses.kjv: And I will betroth thee unto me for ever; yea, I will betroth thee unto me in righteousness, and in judgment, and in lovingkindness, and in mercies.

verses.text: And if you pour out your soul to the hungry, and satisfy the afflicted soul, then your light will rise in darkness, and your obscurity will be as the noonday…
verses.meaning: Give yourself to feeding the hungry and helping the hurting, and your own dark days will start to brighten.
verses.kjv: And if thou draw out thy soul to the hungry, and satisfy the afflicted soul; then shall thy light rise in obscurity, and thy darkness be as the noonday…

verses.text: For thus said the Lord GOD, the Holy One of Israel, “You will be saved in returning and rest. Your strength will be in quietness and in confidence.” You refused…
verses.meaning: God offered strength through returning, rest and quiet trust, but his people refused. Don’t miss it.
verses.kjv: For thus saith the Lord GOD, the Holy One of Israel; In returning and rest shall ye be saved; in quietness and in confidence shall be your strength: and ye would not.

verses.text: For the vision is yet for the appointed time, and it hurries toward the end, and won’t prove false. Though it takes time, wait for it, because it will surely come. It won’t delay.
verses.meaning: God’s promises keep their own schedule. If it seems slow, keep waiting: it will surely come.
verses.kjv: For the vision is yet for an appointed time, but at the end it shall speak, and not lie: though it tarry, wait for it; because it will surely come, it will not tarry.

verses.text: I will sprinkle clean water on you, and you will be clean. I will cleanse you from all your filthiness and from all your idols.
verses.meaning: God promises a fresh start: he scrubs away the grime of sin and every idol you’ve leaned on.
verses.kjv: Then will I sprinkle clean water upon you, and ye shall be clean: from all your filthiness, and from all your idols, will I cleanse you.

verses.text: Then Jesus said to them, “Don’t be afraid. Go tell my brothers that they should go into Galilee, and there they will see me.”
verses.meaning: The risen Jesus calmed the women’s fear and gave them a job: go and tell. Courage often follows a call.
verses.kjv: Then said Jesus unto them, Be not afraid: go tell my brethren that they go into Galilee, and there shall they see me.

verses.text: He who tills his land shall have plenty of bread, but he who chases fantasies is void of understanding.
verses.meaning: Real, steady work bears fruit, but chasing daydreams leaves you empty. Some scrolling is exactly that chase.
verses.kjv: He that tilleth his land shall be satisfied with bread: but he that followeth vain persons is void of understanding.

verses.text: Behold, I have engraved you on the palms of my hands. Your walls are continually before me.
verses.meaning: God says he’s carved you into the palms of his hands. You’re always right in front of him.
verses.kjv: Behold, I have graven thee upon the palms of my hands; thy walls are continually before me.

verses.text: So he set it before them and they ate and had some left over, according to the LORD’s word.
verses.meaning: Twenty small loaves fed a hundred people with some left over. In God’s hands, a little can go a long way.
verses.kjv: So he set it before them, and they did eat, and left thereof, according to the word of the LORD.

verses.text: As one who takes away a garment in cold weather, or vinegar on soda, so is one who sings songs to a heavy heart.
verses.meaning: Forced cheer can sting a grieving friend. Sometimes love means sitting gently with their sadness.
verses.kjv: As he that taketh away a garment in cold weather, and as vinegar upon nitre, so is he that singeth songs to an heavy heart.

verses.text: For lack of wood a fire goes out. Without gossip, a quarrel dies down.
verses.meaning: Fights need fuel. Stop passing on gossip, and many quarrels simply burn out.
verses.kjv: Where no wood is, there the fire goeth out: so where there is no talebearer, the strife ceaseth.

verses.text: Yet, looking to the promise of God, he didn’t waver through unbelief, but grew strong through faith, giving glory to God…
verses.meaning: Abraham didn’t pretend the odds were good. He kept looking at God’s promise, and his faith grew stronger.
verses.kjv: He staggered not at the promise of God through unbelief; but was strong in faith, giving glory to God…

verses.text: She called the name of the LORD who spoke to her, “You are a God who sees,” for she said, “Have I even stayed alive after seeing him?”
verses.meaning: Hagar, alone and mistreated, found out God had seen her all along. He sees you too.
verses.kjv: And she called the name of the LORD that spake unto her, Thou God seest me: for she said, Have I also here looked after him that seeth me?

verses.text: But I will sacrifice to you with the voice of thanksgiving. I will pay that which I have vowed. Salvation belongs to the LORD.
verses.meaning: Jonah gave thanks while still inside the fish. You can thank God before you see the rescue.
verses.kjv: But I will sacrifice unto thee with the voice of thanksgiving; I will pay that that I have vowed. Salvation is of the LORD.

verses.text: But I tell you, love your enemies, bless those who curse you, do good to those who hate you, and pray for those who mistreat you and persecute you…
verses.meaning: Jesus asks for the hardest kind of love: praying for and doing good to people who wish you harm.
verses.kjv: But I say unto you, Love your enemies, bless them that curse you, do good to them that hate you, and pray for them which despitefully use you, and persecute you…

verses.text: And when you turn to the right hand, and when you turn to the left, your ears will hear a voice behind you, saying, “This is the way. Walk in it.”
verses.meaning: Whichever way you turn, God can still steer you. Stay close enough to hear him say which way to walk.
verses.kjv: And thine ears shall hear a word behind thee, saying, This is the way, walk ye in it, when ye turn to the right hand, and when ye turn to the left.

verses.text: As the livestock that go down into the valley, the LORD’s Spirit caused them to rest. So you led your people to make yourself a glorious name.
verses.meaning: God’s Spirit gives rest the way a herder leads cattle down into a calm, grassy valley.
verses.kjv: As a beast goeth down into the valley, the Spirit of the LORD caused him to rest: so didst thou lead thy people, to make thyself a glorious name.

verses.text: But to you who fear my name shall the sun of righteousness arise with healing in its wings. You will go out and leap like calves of the stall.
verses.meaning: For people who honor God, a new day is coming like sunrise, with healing and joy that makes you leap.
verses.kjv: But unto you that fear my name shall the Sun of righteousness arise with healing in his wings; and ye shall go forth, and grow up as calves of the stall.

verses.text: To the Lord our God belong mercies and forgiveness, for we have rebelled against him.
verses.meaning: Daniel was honest about his people’s rebellion and still prayed boldly, because God is the one who forgives.
verses.kjv: To the Lord our God belong mercies and forgivenesses, though we have rebelled against him…

verses.text: He went forward a little, fell on his face, and prayed, saying, “My Father, if it is possible, let this cup pass away from me; nevertheless, not what I desire, but what you desire.”
verses.meaning: Jesus was honest that he dreaded the suffering ahead, then chose his Father’s will anyway.
verses.kjv: And he went a little further, and fell on his face, and prayed, saying, O my Father, if it be possible, let this cup pass from me: nevertheless not as I will, but as thou wilt.

verses.text: A simple man believes everything, but the prudent man carefully considers his ways.
verses.meaning: Not everything you read is true. A wise person slows down and thinks before acting on it.
verses.kjv: The simple believeth every word: but the prudent man looketh well to his going.

verses.text: You will also be a crown of beauty in the LORD’s hand, and a royal diadem in your God’s hand. You will not be called Forsaken any more, nor will your land be called Desolate any more; but you will be called Hephzibah, and your land Beulah; for the LORD delights in you, and your land will be married.
verses.meaning: God renames his people: no longer Forsaken, but his delight. He holds you like a royal crown.
verses.kjv: Thou shalt also be a crown of glory in the hand of the LORD, and a royal diadem in the hand of thy God. Thou shalt no more be termed Forsaken; neither shall thy land any more be termed Desolate: but thou shalt be called Hephzi-bah, and thy land Beulah: for the LORD delighteth in thee, and thy land shall be married.

verses.text: Yes, forty years you sustained them in the wilderness. They lacked nothing. Their clothes didn’t grow old, and their feet didn’t swell.
verses.meaning: Clothes didn’t wear out and feet didn’t swell in forty desert years. God cares about the small details.
verses.kjv: Yea, forty years didst thou sustain them in the wilderness, so that they lacked nothing; their clothes waxed not old, and their feet swelled not.

verses.text: The wounds of a friend are faithful, although the kisses of an enemy are profuse.
verses.meaning: A true friend will tell you hard truths. Flattery feels nice, but honest love is worth more.
verses.kjv: Faithful are the wounds of a friend; but the kisses of an enemy are deceitful.

verses.text: The words of the wise heard in quiet are better than the cry of him who rules among fools.
verses.meaning: Calm, wise words carry further than shouting. You don’t have to be the loudest to be heard.
verses.kjv: The words of wise men are heard in quiet more than the cry of him that ruleth among fools.

verses.text: Now we who are strong ought to bear the weaknesses of the weak, and not to please ourselves.
verses.meaning: If you’re strong right now, use that strength to help carry someone who’s struggling.
verses.kjv: We then that are strong ought to bear the infirmities of the weak, and not to please ourselves.

verses.text: The LORD appeared to him the same night, and said, “I am the God of Abraham your father. Don’t be afraid, for I am with you, and will bless you, and multiply your offspring for my servant Abraham’s sake.”
verses.meaning: God met Isaac at night after a tense stretch: don’t be afraid, I’m with you, just as I was with your father.
verses.kjv: And the LORD appeared unto him the same night, and said, I am the God of Abraham thy father: fear not, for I am with thee, and will bless thee, and multiply thy seed for my servant Abraham’s sake.

verses.text: In that day you will say, “I will give thanks to you, the LORD; for though you were angry with me, your anger has turned away and you comfort me.”
verses.meaning: Where you deserved anger, God offers comfort. That turnaround is something to thank him for every day.
verses.kjv: And in that day thou shalt say, O LORD, I will praise thee: though thou wast angry with me, thine anger is turned away, and thou comfortedst me.

verses.text: But when he saw the multitudes, he was moved with compassion for them because they were harassed and scattered, like sheep without a shepherd.
verses.meaning: Jesus looked at tired, lost crowds and his heart went out to them. He sees you with that same compassion.
verses.kjv: But when he saw the multitudes, he was moved with compassion on them, because they fainted, and were scattered abroad, as sheep having no shepherd.

verses.text: Learn to do well. Seek justice. Relieve the oppressed. Defend the fatherless. Plead for the widow.
verses.meaning: Doing good is a skill you learn. God points it at people who have no one to stand up for them.
verses.kjv: Learn to do well; seek judgment, relieve the oppressed, judge the fatherless, plead for the widow.

verses.text: The LORD says, “Stand in the ways and see, and ask for the old paths, ‘Where is the good way?’ and walk in it, and you will find rest for your souls. But they said, ‘We will not walk in it.’”
verses.meaning: Feeling lost? Ask for God’s good, old path and walk in it. That’s where your soul finds rest.
verses.kjv: Thus saith the LORD, Stand ye in the ways, and see, and ask for the old paths, where is the good way, and walk therein, and ye shall find rest for your souls. But they said, We will not walk therein.

verses.text: I will restore to you the years that the swarming locust has eaten, the great locust, the grasshopper, and the caterpillar, my great army, which I sent among you.
verses.meaning: God promised to give back the years Israel lost. He can bring good out of seasons that felt wasted.
verses.kjv: And I will restore to you the years that the locust hath eaten, the cankerworm, and the caterpiller, and the palmerworm, my great army which I sent among you.

verses.text: He prayed to the LORD, and said, “Please, LORD, wasn’t this what I said when I was still in my own country? Therefore I hurried to flee to Tarshish, for I knew that you are a gracious God and merciful, slow to anger, and abundant in loving kindness, and you relent of doing harm.”
verses.meaning: Jonah ran because he knew God would forgive even his enemies. God’s mercy is bigger than our grudges.
verses.kjv: And he prayed unto the LORD, and said, I pray thee, O LORD, was not this my saying, when I was yet in my country? Therefore I fled before unto Tarshish: for I knew that thou art a gracious God, and merciful, slow to anger, and of great kindness, and repentest thee of the evil.

verses.text: Jesus stood still and said, “Call him.” They called the blind man, saying to him, “Cheer up! Get up. He is calling you!”
verses.meaning: The crowd that hushed blind Bartimaeus now told him to take heart: Jesus was calling him over.
verses.kjv: And Jesus stood still, and commanded him to be called. And they call the blind man, saying unto him, Be of good comfort, rise; he calleth thee.

verses.text: The heart of one who has understanding seeks knowledge, but the mouths of fools feed on folly.
verses.meaning: A wise heart goes looking for real understanding, while fools snack on nonsense. Watch what you feed on.
verses.kjv: The heart of him that hath understanding seeketh knowledge: but the mouth of fools feedeth on foolishness.

verses.text: I will give them a heart to know me, that I am the LORD. They will be my people, and I will be their God; for they will return to me with their whole heart.
verses.meaning: God gives his people a heart to know him. You belong to him, and he gladly calls himself your God.
verses.kjv: And I will give them an heart to know me, that I am the LORD: and they shall be my people, and I will be their God: for they shall return unto me with their whole heart.

verses.text: Who provides for the raven his prey, when his young ones cry to God, and wander for lack of food?
verses.meaning: God reminds Job that he feeds the hungry chicks of ravens. If he notices them, he hasn’t overlooked you.
verses.kjv: Who provideth for the raven his food? when his young ones cry unto God, they wander for lack of meat.

verses.text: Perfume and incense bring joy to the heart; so does earnest counsel from a man’s friend.
verses.meaning: Heartfelt advice from a friend is as refreshing as a sweet fragrance. Keep wise friends close.
verses.kjv: Ointment and perfume rejoice the heart: so doth the sweetness of a man’s friend by hearty counsel.

verses.text: He will judge between the nations, and will decide concerning many peoples. They shall beat their swords into plowshares, and their spears into pruning hooks. Nation shall not lift up sword against nation, neither shall they learn war any more.
verses.meaning: God’s coming peace is so complete that weapons get turned into farm tools, and war isn’t even taught.
verses.kjv: And he shall judge among the nations, and shall rebuke many people: and they shall beat their swords into plowshares, and their spears into pruninghooks: nation shall not lift up sword against nation, neither shall they learn war any more.

verses.text: For he was crucified through weakness, yet he lives through the power of God. For we also are weak in him, but we will live with him through the power of God toward you.
verses.meaning: Jesus looked weak on the cross, yet he lives by God’s power. That same power is at work in weak people.
verses.kjv: For though he was crucified through weakness, yet he liveth by the power of God. For we also are weak in him, but we shall live with him by the power of God toward you.

verses.text: The LORD said, “I have surely seen the affliction of my people who are in Egypt, and have heard their cry because of their taskmasters, for I know their sorrows.”
verses.meaning: God told Moses he had seen his people’s misery and heard their cries. He knows your sorrows too.
verses.kjv: And the LORD said, I have surely seen the affliction of my people which are in Egypt, and have heard their cry by reason of their taskmasters; for I know their sorrows…

verses.text: Land, don’t be afraid. Be glad and rejoice, for the LORD has done great things.
verses.meaning: After a season of ruin, the prophet speaks to the scorched land itself: be glad, God has done great things.
verses.kjv: Fear not, O land; be glad and rejoice: for the LORD will do great things.

verses.text: Jesus said to him, “‘You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your mind.’ This is the first and great commandment. A second likewise is this, ‘You shall love your neighbor as yourself.’”
verses.meaning: Jesus boiled faith down to two loves: God with everything you are, and your neighbor as yourself.
verses.kjv: Jesus said unto him, Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind. This is the first and great commandment. And the second is like unto it, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself.

verses.text: When the vessel that he made of the clay was marred in the hand of the potter, he made it again another vessel, as seemed good to the potter to make it.
verses.meaning: When the clay was marred, the potter didn’t toss it; he reshaped it. God can remake a life that went wrong.
verses.kjv: And the vessel that he made of clay was marred in the hand of the potter: so he made it again another vessel, as seemed good to the potter to make it.

verses.text: On this I awakened, and saw; and my sleep was sweet to me.
verses.meaning: After a vision of God’s restoring promises, Jeremiah woke up and found his sleep had been sweet.
verses.kjv: Upon this I awaked, and beheld; and my sleep was sweet unto me.

verses.text: I set my rainbow in the cloud, and it will be a sign of a covenant between me and the earth.
verses.meaning: After the flood, God set a rainbow in the sky as a sign of his promise. He keeps his word.
verses.kjv: I do set my bow in the cloud, and it shall be for a token of a covenant between me and the earth.

verses.text: He will again have compassion on us. He will tread our iniquities under foot. You will cast all their sins into the depths of the sea.
verses.meaning: God doesn’t just set your sins aside. He hurls them into the deepest sea, out of reach for good.
verses.kjv: He will turn again, he will have compassion upon us; he will subdue our iniquities; and thou wilt cast all their sins into the depths of the sea.

verses.text: Joseph of Arimathaea, a prominent council member who also himself was looking for God’s Kingdom, came. He boldly went in to Pilate, and asked for Jesus’ body.
verses.meaning: Joseph risked his reputation to ask Pilate for Jesus’s body. Honoring Jesus can take quiet bravery.
verses.kjv: Joseph of Arimathaea, an honourable counsellor, which also waited for the kingdom of God, came, and went in boldly unto Pilate, and craved the body of Jesus.

verses.text: Wisdom is before the face of one who has understanding, but the eyes of a fool wander to the ends of the earth.
verses.meaning: Wise people keep wisdom right in front of them. Foolish eyes wander everywhere, like an endless feed.
verses.kjv: Wisdom is before him that hath understanding; but the eyes of a fool are in the ends of the earth.

verses.text: I will sow her to me in the earth; and I will have mercy on her who had not obtained mercy; and I will tell those who were not my people, ‘You are my people;’ and they will say, ‘You are My God!’
verses.meaning: God turns outsiders into family. People once called “not my people” now hear him call them his own.
verses.kjv: And I will sow her unto me in the earth; and I will have mercy upon her that had not obtained mercy; and I will say to them which were not my people, Thou art my people; and they shall say, Thou art my God.

verses.text: Remove far from me falsehood and lies. Give me neither poverty nor riches. Feed me with the food that is needful for me…
verses.meaning: A wise prayer: spare me both want and excess, and feed me what I need today. Enough is a gift.
verses.kjv: Remove far from me vanity and lies: give me neither poverty nor riches; feed me with food convenient for me…

verses.text: Don’t forsake your friend and your father’s friend. Don’t go to your brother’s house in the day of your disaster. A neighbor who is near is better than a distant brother.
verses.meaning: Keep old friendships alive, even your family’s friends. In a crisis, a neighbor close by can help most.
verses.kjv: Thine own friend, and thy father’s friend, forsake not; neither go into thy brother’s house in the day of thy calamity: for better is a neighbour that is near than a brother far off.

verses.text: The wolf will live with the lamb, and the leopard will lie down with the young goat, the calf, the young lion, and the fattened calf together; and a little child will lead them.
verses.meaning: In God’s coming kingdom, natural enemies rest side by side. His peace will reach even the wild things.
verses.kjv: The wolf also shall dwell with the lamb, and the leopard shall lie down with the kid; and the calf and the young lion and the fatling together; and a little child shall lead them.

verses.text: An angel from heaven appeared to him, strengthening him.
verses.meaning: Even Jesus, praying in anguish the night before the cross, was given strength from heaven to keep going.
verses.kjv: And there appeared an angel unto him from heaven, strengthening him.

verses.text: I am not able to bear all this people alone, because it is too heavy for me.
verses.meaning: Even Moses told God, “This is too heavy for me alone.” God answered by giving him people to share the load.
verses.kjv: I am not able to bear all this people alone, because it is too heavy for me.

verses.text: At that time, Jesus answered, “I thank you, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, that you hid these things from the wise and understanding, and revealed them to infants.”
verses.meaning: Jesus thanked the Father that God is known by childlike trust, not cleverness. That’s good news for everyone.
verses.kjv: At that time Jesus answered and said, I thank thee, O Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because thou hast hid these things from the wise and prudent, and hast revealed them unto babes.

verses.text: Being moved with compassion, he stretched out his hand, and touched him, and said to him, “I want to. Be made clean.”
verses.meaning: Jesus touched a man everyone else avoided. His love reaches the people others keep at a distance.
verses.kjv: And Jesus, moved with compassion, put forth his hand, and touched him, and saith unto him, I will; be thou clean.

verses.text: The LORD’s word came to Jonah the second time, saying, “Arise, go to Nineveh, that great city, and preach to it the message that I give you.”
verses.meaning: Jonah ran from his calling, and God came back with it a second time. Running once doesn’t rule you out.
verses.kjv: And the word of the LORD came unto Jonah the second time, saying, Arise, go unto Nineveh, that great city, and preach unto it the preaching that I bid thee.

verses.text: Therefore don’t be afraid, O Jacob my servant, says the LORD. Don’t be dismayed, Israel. For, behold, I will save you from afar, and save your offspring from the land of their captivity. Jacob will return, and will be quiet and at ease. No one will make him afraid.
verses.meaning: God promised his scattered people they’d come home to quiet and ease, with no one left to fear.
verses.kjv: Therefore fear thou not, O my servant Jacob, saith the LORD; neither be dismayed, O Israel: for, lo, I will save thee from afar, and thy seed from the land of their captivity; and Jacob shall return, and shall be in rest, and be quiet, and none shall make him afraid.

verses.text: He raises up the poor out of the dust. He lifts up the needy from the dunghill to make them sit with princes and inherit the throne of glory. For the pillars of the earth are the LORD’s. He has set the world on them.
verses.meaning: Hannah sang about a God who lifts people up from the dust. Being low now doesn’t mean you’re forgotten.
verses.kjv: He raiseth up the poor out of the dust, and lifteth up the beggar from the dunghill, to set them among princes, and to make them inherit the throne of glory: for the pillars of the earth are the LORD’s, and he hath set the world upon them.

verses.text: He answered and spoke to those who stood before him, saying, “Take the filthy garments off him.” To him he said, “Behold, I have caused your iniquity to pass from you, and I will clothe you with rich clothing.”
verses.meaning: In a vision, God takes a priest’s filthy clothes off and dresses him in rich ones. Guilt gone, honor given.
verses.kjv: And he answered and spake unto those that stood before him, saying, Take away the filthy garments from him. And unto him he said, Behold, I have caused thine iniquity to pass from thee, and I will clothe thee with change of raiment.

verses.text: Jesus therefore, knowing all the things that were happening to him, went out and said to them, “Who are you looking for?”
verses.meaning: Jesus knew exactly what was coming, yet he stepped forward to meet the soldiers instead of hiding.
verses.kjv: Jesus therefore, knowing all things that should come upon him, went forth, and said unto them, Whom seek ye?

verses.text: My son, give me your heart; and let your eyes keep in my ways.
verses.meaning: A loving father asks for his child’s heart and attention. God asks for yours, and your eyes follow your heart.
verses.kjv: My son, give me thine heart, and let thine eyes observe my ways.

verses.text: When Israel was a child, then I loved him, and called my son out of Egypt.
verses.meaning: God remembers loving Israel as a little child and calling his son out of slavery. His love starts early.
verses.kjv: When Israel was a child, then I loved him, and called my son out of Egypt.

verses.text: The liberal soul shall be made fat. He who waters shall be watered also himself.
verses.meaning: Generosity has a way of coming back around. When you refresh others, you often find yourself refreshed.
verses.kjv: The liberal soul shall be made fat: and he that watereth shall be watered also himself.

verses.text: Isn’t it to distribute your bread to the hungry, and that you bring the poor who are cast out to your house? When you see the naked, that you cover him; and that you not hide yourself from your own flesh?
verses.meaning: The worship God wants looks like sharing your food, opening your home and not ignoring your own family.
verses.kjv: Is it not to deal thy bread to the hungry, and that thou bring the poor that are cast out to thy house? when thou seest the naked, that thou cover him; and that thou hide not thyself from thine own flesh?

verses.text: Oh that you had listened to my commandments! Then your peace would have been like a river and your righteousness like the waves of the sea.
verses.meaning: God longs for you to have peace that flows like a river. Following his ways is how it reaches you.
verses.kjv: O that thou hadst hearkened to my commandments! then had thy peace been as a river, and thy righteousness as the waves of the sea…

verses.text: He also spoke a parable to them that they must always pray and not give up…
verses.meaning: Jesus told a whole story to make one point: keep praying, and don’t quit when answers take time.
verses.kjv: And he spake a parable unto them to this end, that men ought always to pray, and not to faint…

verses.text: And in the wilderness where you have seen how that the LORD your God carried you, as a man carries his son, in all the way that you went, until you came to this place.
verses.meaning: Looking back, you may see that God carried you through, the way a parent carries a tired child.
verses.kjv: And in the wilderness, where thou hast seen how that the LORD thy God bare thee, as a man doth bear his son, in all the way that ye went, until ye came into this place.

verses.text: He didn’t allow him, but said to him, “Go to your house, to your friends, and tell them what great things the Lord has done for you and how he had mercy on you.”
verses.meaning: Jesus sent the man he’d set free home with a job: tell your people what God did. Gratitude loves to share.
verses.kjv: Howbeit Jesus suffered him not, but saith unto him, Go home to thy friends, and tell them how great things the Lord hath done for thee, and hath had compassion on thee.

verses.text: Jesus looking at him loved him, and said to him, “One thing you lack. Go, sell whatever you have and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven; and come, follow me, taking up the cross.”
verses.meaning: Jesus loved this man before he challenged him. His hardest words come from love, not disapproval.
verses.kjv: Then Jesus beholding him loved him, and said unto him, One thing thou lackest: go thy way, sell whatsoever thou hast, and give to the poor, and thou shalt have treasure in heaven: and come, take up the cross, and follow me.

verses.text: He said to them, “Come after me, and I will make you fishers for men.”
verses.meaning: Jesus called ordinary fishermen to follow him, and he’d shape them into people who bring others to God.
verses.kjv: And he saith unto them, Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men.

verses.text: “I myself will be the shepherd of my sheep, and I will cause them to lie down,” says the Lord GOD.
verses.meaning: God himself is the shepherd who makes his sheep lie down. Your rest matters to him.
verses.kjv: I will feed my flock, and I will cause them to lie down, saith the Lord GOD.

verses.text: Nothing failed of any good thing which the LORD had spoken to the house of Israel. All came to pass.
verses.meaning: Not one of God’s good promises to Israel fell through. Every single one came true.
verses.kjv: There failed not ought of any good thing which the LORD had spoken unto the house of Israel; all came to pass.

verses.text: Forgive us our debts, as we also forgive our debtors.
verses.meaning: Jesus taught you to ask for forgiveness and to give it in the same breath. Both belong in daily prayer.
verses.kjv: And forgive us our debts, as we forgive our debtors.

verses.text: Now when they saw the boldness of Peter and John, and had perceived that they were unlearned and ignorant men, they marveled. They recognized that they had been with Jesus.
verses.meaning: Peter and John had no fancy training, but time with Jesus made them bold. That’s still how it works.
verses.kjv: Now when they saw the boldness of Peter and John, and perceived that they were unlearned and ignorant men, they marvelled; and they took knowledge of them, that they had been with Jesus.

verses.text: Have you found honey? Eat as much as is sufficient for you, lest you eat too much, and vomit it.
verses.meaning: Even honey makes you sick if you overdo it. Good things still need limits, screens included.
verses.kjv: Hast thou found honey? eat so much as is sufficient for thee, lest thou be filled therewith, and vomit it.

verses.text: “They shall be mine,” says the LORD of Armies, “my own possession in the day that I make. I will spare them, as a man spares his own son who serves him.”
verses.meaning: God calls the people who honor him his treasured possession, cared for the way a father cares for his son.
verses.kjv: And they shall be mine, saith the LORD of hosts, in that day when I make up my jewels; and I will spare them, as a man spareth his own son that serveth him.

verses.text: He who has pity on the poor lends to the LORD; he will reward him.
verses.meaning: Kindness to someone poor is never wasted. God counts it as a loan to himself, and he never forgets.
verses.kjv: He that hath pity upon the poor lendeth unto the LORD; and that which he hath given will he pay him again.

verses.text: Thus has the LORD of Armies spoken, saying, ‘Execute true judgment, and show kindness and compassion every man to his brother. Don’t oppress the widow, the fatherless, the foreigner, nor the poor; and let none of you devise evil against his brother in your heart.’
verses.meaning: God wants fairness and kindness between people, special care for the vulnerable and no hidden schemes.
verses.kjv: Thus speaketh the LORD of hosts, saying, Execute true judgment, and shew mercy and compassions every man to his brother: And oppress not the widow, nor the fatherless, the stranger, nor the poor; and let none of you imagine evil against his brother in your heart.

verses.text: All your children will be taught by the LORD, and your children’s peace will be great.
verses.meaning: God’s promise to restore his people included their children: taught by God himself and deeply at peace.
verses.kjv: And all thy children shall be taught of the LORD; and great shall be the peace of thy children.

verses.text: But you will receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you. You will be witnesses to me in Jerusalem, in all Judea and Samaria, and to the uttermost parts of the earth.
verses.meaning: The Holy Spirit gives ordinary people the power to tell others about Jesus, close to home and far away.
verses.kjv: But ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you: and ye shall be witnesses unto me both in Jerusalem, and in all Judæa, and in Samaria, and unto the uttermost part of the earth.

verses.text: Hannah answered, “No, my lord, I am a woman of a sorrowful spirit. I have not been drinking wine or strong drink, but I poured out my soul before the LORD.”
verses.meaning: Hannah didn’t hide her sorrow; she poured it all out before God. You’re free to do the same.
verses.kjv: And Hannah answered and said, No, my lord, I am a woman of a sorrowful spirit: I have drunk neither wine nor strong drink, but have poured out my soul before the LORD.

verses.text: For he who is mighty has done great things for me. Holy is his name.
verses.meaning: Young and unknown, Mary sang of the great things God had done for her. What has he done for you?
verses.kjv: For he that is mighty hath done to me great things; and holy is his name.

verses.text: But love your enemies, and do good, and lend, expecting nothing back; and your reward will be great, and you will be children of the Most High; for he is kind toward the unthankful and evil.
verses.meaning: Love people who don’t deserve it and give without keeping score. That’s how God treats everyone.
verses.kjv: But love ye your enemies, and do good, and lend, hoping for nothing again; and your reward shall be great, and ye shall be the children of the Highest: for he is kind unto the unthankful and to the evil.

verses.text: Let your Kingdom come. Let your will be done on earth as it is in heaven.
verses.meaning: Jesus taught you to pray for God’s will here and now, not just someday. Your day can be part of the answer.
verses.kjv: Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done in earth, as it is in heaven.

verses.text: ‘I will make with them a covenant of peace, and will cause evil animals to cease out of the land. They will dwell securely in the wilderness and sleep in the woods.’
verses.meaning: God’s covenant of peace pictured people so safe they could fall asleep even out in the woods.
verses.kjv: And I will make with them a covenant of peace, and will cause the evil beasts to cease out of the land: and they shall dwell safely in the wilderness, and sleep in the woods.

verses.text: God is not a man, that he should lie, nor a son of man, that he should repent. Has he said, and he won’t do it? Or has he spoken, and he won’t make it good?
verses.meaning: People break promises; God doesn’t. What he says, he does, so you can lean on his word.
verses.kjv: God is not a man, that he should lie; neither the son of man, that he should repent: hath he said, and shall he not do it? or hath he spoken, and shall he not make it good?

verses.text: Behold, they brought to him a man who was paralyzed, lying on a bed. Jesus, seeing their faith, said to the paralytic, “Son, cheer up! Your sins are forgiven you.”
verses.meaning: Friends carried a paralyzed man to Jesus, and the first thing Jesus gave him was courage and forgiveness.
verses.kjv: And, behold, they brought to him a man sick of the palsy, lying on a bed: and Jesus seeing their faith said unto the sick of the palsy; Son, be of good cheer; thy sins be forgiven thee.

verses.text: The Lord said to Paul in the night by a vision, “Don’t be afraid, but speak and don’t be silent; for I am with you, and no one will attack you to harm you, for I have many people in this city.”
verses.meaning: Paul was told not to go quiet out of fear: keep speaking, because God was with him in that city.
verses.kjv: Then spake the Lord to Paul in the night by a vision, Be not afraid, but speak, and hold not thy peace: For I am with thee, and no man shall set on thee to hurt thee: for I have much people in this city.

verses.text: Sheol and Abaddon are never satisfied; and a man’s eyes are never satisfied.
verses.meaning: Eyes are never full. There’s always one more video, so contentment comes from choosing to stop.
verses.kjv: Hell and destruction are never full; so the eyes of man are never satisfied.

verses.text: But when Jesus saw it, he was moved with indignation and said to them, “Allow the little children to come to me! Don’t forbid them, for God’s Kingdom belongs to such as these.”
verses.meaning: Jesus was upset when kids were shooed away. His kingdom belongs to people who come to him like children.
verses.kjv: But when Jesus saw it, he was much displeased, and said unto them, Suffer the little children to come unto me, and forbid them not: for of such is the kingdom of God.

verses.text: Hey! Come, everyone who thirsts, to the waters! Come, he who has no money, buy, and eat! Yes, come, buy wine and milk without money and without price.
verses.meaning: God’s invitation has no price tag. Come thirsty, even with empty pockets, and receive what money can’t buy.
verses.kjv: Ho, every one that thirsteth, come ye to the waters, and he that hath no money; come ye, buy, and eat; yea, come, buy wine and milk without money and without price.

verses.text: Then those who feared the LORD spoke one with another; and the LORD listened and heard, and a book of memory was written before him for those who feared the LORD and who honored his name.
verses.meaning: When believers talk together about God, he leans in to listen and remembers them.
verses.kjv: Then they that feared the LORD spake often one to another: and the LORD hearkened, and heard it, and a book of remembrance was written before him for them that feared the LORD, and that thought upon his name.

verses.text: “I create the fruit of the lips: Peace, peace, to him who is far off and to him who is near,” says the LORD; “and I will heal them.”
verses.meaning: God speaks peace to people near him and people who feel far away. No one is too far gone for him.
verses.kjv: I create the fruit of the lips; Peace, peace to him that is far off, and to him that is near, saith the LORD; and I will heal him.

verses.text: I know your works (behold, I have set before you an open door, which no one can shut), that you have a little power, and kept my word, and didn’t deny my name.
verses.meaning: You don’t need a lot of strength to be faithful. Jesus sees the little you have and holds a door open for you.
verses.kjv: I know thy works: behold, I have set before thee an open door, and no man can shut it: for thou hast a little strength, and hast kept my word, and hast not denied my name.

verses.text: In my distress, I called on the LORD. Yes, I called to my God. He heard my voice out of his temple. My cry came into his ears.
verses.meaning: David cried out from deep distress, and God heard him. Your cry for help reaches God’s ears.
verses.kjv: In my distress I called upon the LORD, and cried to my God: and he did hear my voice out of his temple, and my cry did enter into his ears.

verses.text: The shepherds returned, glorifying and praising God for all the things that they had heard and seen, just as it was told them.
verses.meaning: The shepherds went back to the same fields, but they went back praising. Thankfulness changes ordinary days.
verses.kjv: And the shepherds returned, glorifying and praising God for all the things that they had heard and seen, as it was told unto them.

verses.text: Now Jesus loved Martha, and her sister, and Lazarus.
verses.meaning: Jesus loved Martha, Mary and Lazarus, even when his timing confused them. Delay isn’t a lack of love.
verses.kjv: Now Jesus loved Martha, and her sister, and Lazarus.

verses.text: For whoever desires to save his life will lose it, and whoever will lose his life for my sake will find it.
verses.meaning: Clutch your life for yourself and you lose it. Give it to Jesus and you find what life was meant to be.
verses.kjv: For whosoever will save his life shall lose it: and whosoever will lose his life for my sake shall find it.

verses.text: But every man will sit under his vine and under his fig tree. No one will make them afraid, for the mouth of the LORD of Armies has spoken.
verses.meaning: God’s future: everyone sitting in the shade of their own vine and fig tree, with nothing to fear.
verses.kjv: But they shall sit every man under his vine and under his fig tree; and none shall make them afraid: for the mouth of the LORD of hosts hath spoken it.

verses.text: But the path of the righteous is like the dawning light that shines more and more until the perfect day.
verses.meaning: Walking God’s way is like watching the sunrise: the light grows a little brighter every day.
verses.kjv: But the path of the just is as the shining light, that shineth more and more unto the perfect day.

verses.text: Then Peter came and said to him, “Lord, how often shall my brother sin against me, and I forgive him? Until seven times?” Jesus said to him, “I don’t tell you until seven times, but, until seventy times seven.”
verses.meaning: Peter offered to forgive seven times. Jesus said to stop counting: forgiveness isn’t something you ration.
verses.kjv: Then came Peter to him, and said, Lord, how oft shall my brother sin against me, and I forgive him? till seven times? Jesus saith unto him, I say not unto thee, Until seven times: but, Until seventy times seven.

verses.text: Therefore, sirs, cheer up! For I believe God, that it will be just as it has been spoken to me.
verses.meaning: In a storm that would wreck the ship, Paul told everyone to take heart because he trusted what God said.
verses.kjv: Wherefore, sirs, be of good cheer: for I believe God, that it shall be even as it was told me.

verses.text: All things are full of weariness beyond uttering. The eye is not satisfied with seeing, nor the ear filled with hearing.
verses.meaning: The eye never gets enough seeing, and the ear never gets enough hearing. More content won’t fill you.
verses.kjv: All things are full of labour; man cannot utter it: the eye is not satisfied with seeing, nor the ear filled with hearing.

verses.text: Nevertheless, don’t rejoice in this, that the spirits are subject to you, but rejoice that your names are written in heaven.
verses.meaning: Jesus said results aren’t your real reason for joy. Your name is written in heaven, and that’s enough.
verses.kjv: Notwithstanding in this rejoice not, that the spirits are subject unto you; but rather rejoice, because your names are written in heaven.

verses.text: And the LORD will guide you continually, satisfy your soul in dry places, and make your bones strong. You will be like a watered garden, and like a spring of water whose waters don’t fail.
verses.meaning: When you pour yourself out for the hungry, God refreshes you like a garden whose water never runs dry.
verses.kjv: And the LORD shall guide thee continually, and satisfy thy soul in drought, and make fat thy bones: and thou shalt be like a watered garden, and like a spring of water, whose waters fail not.

verses.text: If your brother sins against you, go, show him his fault between you and him alone. If he listens to you, you have gained back your brother.
verses.meaning: If someone wrongs you, talk to them privately first. The goal isn’t winning; it’s getting your friend back.
verses.kjv: Moreover if thy brother shall trespass against thee, go and tell him his fault between thee and him alone: if he shall hear thee, thou hast gained thy brother.

verses.text: Moreover I will make a covenant of peace with them. It will be an everlasting covenant with them. I will place them, multiply them, and will set my sanctuary among them forever more.
verses.meaning: God’s peace isn’t a short truce. He promises a covenant that lasts, and his presence right among his people.
verses.kjv: Moreover I will make a covenant of peace with them; it shall be an everlasting covenant with them: and I will place them, and multiply them, and will set my sanctuary in the midst of them for evermore.

verses.text: You have perseverance and have endured for my name’s sake, and have not grown weary.
verses.meaning: Jesus notices when you keep going for his sake. Your quiet endurance is never invisible to him.
verses.kjv: And hast borne, and hast patience, and for my name’s sake hast laboured, and hast not fainted.

verses.text: He also brought me out into a large place. He delivered me, because he delighted in me.
verses.meaning: God brought David out of a tight spot into wide open space, and the reason was simple: God delighted in him.
verses.kjv: He brought me forth also into a large place: he delivered me, because he delighted in me.
