verses.text: Knowing that you were redeemed, not with corruptible things like silver or gold, from the useless way of life handed down from your fathers, but with precious blood, as of a lamb without blemish or spot, the blood of Christ…
verses.meaning: Your worth isn’t measured in silver or gold. You were bought back with the priceless blood of Jesus.
verses.kjv: Forasmuch as ye know that ye were not redeemed with corruptible things, as silver and gold, from your vain conversation received by tradition from your fathers; But with the precious blood of Christ, as of a lamb without blemish and without spot…

verses.text: The humble shall eat and be satisfied. They shall praise the LORD who seek after him. Let your hearts live forever.
verses.meaning: This psalm moves from feeling abandoned to a feast where the humble eat their fill and praise God.
verses.kjv: The meek shall eat and be satisfied: they shall praise the LORD that seek him: your heart shall live for ever.

verses.text: Remember those who are in bonds, as bound with them, and those who are ill-treated, since you are also in the body.
verses.meaning: Remember people in prison and those being mistreated, as if their pain were your own.
verses.kjv: Remember them that are in bonds, as bound with them; and them which suffer adversity, as being yourselves also in the body.

verses.text: A wrathful man stirs up contention, but one who is slow to anger appeases strife.
verses.meaning: A hothead keeps fights going, but a patient person can calm a room. Be slow to anger.
verses.kjv: A wrathful man stirreth up strife: but he that is slow to anger appeaseth strife.

verses.text: Who remembered us in our low estate, for his loving kindness endures forever…
verses.meaning: God remembered you at your lowest point. That alone is worth thanking him for, and his love never runs out.
verses.kjv: Who remembered us in our low estate: for his mercy endureth for ever…

verses.text: Beloved, if God loved us in this way, we also ought to love one another.
verses.meaning: Receiving God’s love comes with a calling: pass it on to the people around you.
verses.kjv: Beloved, if God so loved us, we ought also to love one another.

verses.text: I glorified you on the earth. I have accomplished the work which you have given me to do.
verses.meaning: Jesus could tell the Father he’d finished the work he was given. Aim to reach your last day able to say that.
verses.kjv: I have glorified thee on the earth: I have finished the work which thou gavest me to do.

verses.text: The LORD says, “The people who survive the sword found favor in the wilderness; even Israel, when I went to cause him to rest.”
verses.meaning: Out in the wilderness, God’s people found grace, and he himself went to give them rest.
verses.kjv: Thus saith the LORD, The people which were left of the sword found grace in the wilderness; even Israel, when I went to cause him to rest.

verses.text: Blessed are those who mourn, for they shall be comforted.
verses.meaning: Jesus calls people who mourn blessed. God sees your grief and promises real comfort.
verses.kjv: Blessed are they that mourn: for they shall be comforted.

verses.text: Looking carefully lest there be any man who falls short of the grace of God, lest any root of bitterness springing up trouble you and many be defiled by it…
verses.meaning: Bitterness grows like a root underground, quietly spreading. Watch for it, and lean on God’s grace.
verses.kjv: Looking diligently lest any man fail of the grace of God; lest any root of bitterness springing up trouble you, and thereby many be defiled…

verses.text: He therefore answered, “I don’t know if he is a sinner. One thing I do know: that though I was blind, now I see.”
verses.meaning: You don’t need every answer to speak up. Like the healed man, you can simply tell what Jesus did for you.
verses.kjv: He answered and said, Whether he be a sinner or no, I know not: one thing I know, that, whereas I was blind, now I see.

verses.text: But solid food is for those who are full grown, who by reason of use have their senses exercised to discern good and evil.
verses.meaning: Discernment grows with practice. Your senses get sharper at spotting good and evil the more you train them.
verses.kjv: But strong meat belongeth to them that are of full age, even those who by reason of use have their senses exercised to discern both good and evil.

verses.text: You also as living stones are built up as a spiritual house, to be a holy priesthood, to offer up spiritual sacrifices, acceptable to God through Jesus Christ.
verses.meaning: You’re a living stone in the house God is building, with a holy part to play in it.
verses.kjv: Ye also, as lively stones, are built up a spiritual house, an holy priesthood, to offer up spiritual sacrifices, acceptable to God by Jesus Christ.

verses.text: I will make them and the places around my hill a blessing. I will cause the shower to come down in its season. There will be showers of blessing.
verses.meaning: God promises rain at the right time. His good gifts come in their season, even when you’re waiting.
verses.kjv: And I will make them and the places round about my hill a blessing; and I will cause the shower to come down in his season; there shall be showers of blessing.

verses.text: Pure religion and undefiled before our God and Father is this: to visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction, and to keep oneself unstained by the world.
verses.meaning: Real faith shows up for orphans and widows in their hard times, and stays true in a messy world.
verses.kjv: Pure religion and undefiled before God and the Father is this, To visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction, and to keep himself unspotted from the world.

verses.text: He has redeemed my soul in peace from the battle that was against me, although there are many who oppose me.
verses.meaning: Many stood against David, yet God brought him through the battle with his soul at peace.
verses.kjv: He hath delivered my soul in peace from the battle that was against me: for there were many with me.

verses.text: No one has seen God at any time. If we love one another, God remains in us, and his love has been perfected in us.
verses.meaning: No one has seen God, but when believers love each other, his love becomes visible and complete in them.
verses.kjv: No man hath seen God at any time. If we love one another, God dwelleth in us, and his love is perfected in us.

verses.text: Who gave himself for us, that he might redeem us from all iniquity and purify for himself a people for his own possession, zealous for good works.
verses.meaning: Jesus gave himself to free you and make you his own people, eager to do good. Eager, not reluctant.
verses.kjv: Who gave himself for us, that he might redeem us from all iniquity, and purify unto himself a peculiar people, zealous of good works.

verses.text: Surely goodness and loving kindness shall follow me all the days of my life, and I will dwell in the LORD’s house forever.
verses.meaning: God’s goodness and love follow you every day, and his house is a home you can settle into for good.
verses.kjv: Surely goodness and mercy shall follow me all the days of my life: and I will dwell in the house of the LORD for ever.

verses.text: When the Lord saw her, he had compassion on her and said to her, “Don’t cry.”
verses.meaning: Jesus saw a grieving widow and his heart went out to her. Your grief moves him too.
verses.kjv: And when the Lord saw her, he had compassion on her, and said unto her, Weep not.

verses.text: For judgment is without mercy to him who has shown no mercy. Mercy triumphs over judgment.
verses.meaning: Showing mercy to others matters deeply. In God’s eyes, mercy wins out over harsh judgment.
verses.kjv: For he shall have judgment without mercy, that hath shewed no mercy; and mercy rejoiceth against judgment.

verses.text: You shall not be scared of them; for the LORD your God is among you, a great and awesome God.
verses.meaning: What’s ahead may look huge, but the God who walks among you is bigger and more powerful still.
verses.kjv: Thou shalt not be affrighted at them: for the LORD thy God is among you, a mighty God and terrible.

verses.text: Looking to Jesus, the author and perfecter of faith, who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising its shame, and has sat down at the right hand of the throne of God.
verses.meaning: Keep your eyes on Jesus, who starts and finishes your faith and endured the cross for the joy ahead.
verses.kjv: Looking unto Jesus the author and finisher of our faith; who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising the shame, and is set down at the right hand of the throne of God.

verses.text: In the past, you were not a people, but now are God’s people, who had not obtained mercy, but now have obtained mercy.
verses.meaning: Once you were outsiders; now you’re God’s own people, and his mercy has found you.
verses.kjv: Which in time past were not a people, but are now the people of God: which had not obtained mercy, but now have obtained mercy.

verses.text: Brothers, if any among you wanders from the truth and someone turns him back, let him know that he who turns a sinner from the error of his way will save a soul from death and will cover a multitude of sins.
verses.meaning: If a friend drifts from the truth, gently helping them back is one of the greatest things you can do.
verses.kjv: Brethren, if any of you do err from the truth, and one convert him; Let him know, that he which converteth the sinner from the error of his way shall save a soul from death, and shall hide a multitude of sins.

verses.text: I will cut off the chariot from Ephraim and the horse from Jerusalem. The battle bow will be cut off; and he will speak peace to the nations. His dominion will be from sea to sea, and from the River to the ends of the earth.
verses.meaning: The humble King God promised would break the weapons of war and speak peace to every nation.
verses.kjv: And I will cut off the chariot from Ephraim, and the horse from Jerusalem, and the battle bow shall be cut off: and he shall speak peace unto the heathen: and his dominion shall be from sea even to sea, and from the river even to the ends of the earth.

verses.text: If a man says, “I love God,” and hates his brother, he is a liar; for he who doesn’t love his brother whom he has seen, how can he love God whom he has not seen?
verses.meaning: Loving God and resenting people don’t mix. Love for an unseen God shows in how you treat people you see.
verses.kjv: If a man say, I love God, and hateth his brother, he is a liar: for he that loveth not his brother whom he hath seen, how can he love God whom he hath not seen?

verses.text: For God is not unrighteous, so as to forget your work and the labor of love which you showed toward his name, in that you served the saints, and still do serve them.
verses.meaning: God doesn’t forget the love you’ve shown by serving his people. No one may thank you, but he remembers.
verses.kjv: For God is not unrighteous to forget your work and labour of love, which ye have shewed toward his name, in that ye have ministered to the saints, and do minister.

verses.text: Israel, hope in the LORD, for there is loving kindness with the LORD. Abundant redemption is with him.
verses.meaning: However far you’ve fallen, hope still makes sense: God’s love is faithful and his rescue is generous.
verses.kjv: Let Israel hope in the LORD: for with the LORD there is mercy, and with him is plenteous redemption.

verses.text: He himself bore our sins in his body on the tree, that we, having died to sins, might live to righteousness. You were healed by his wounds.
verses.meaning: Jesus carried your sins in his own body on the cross, so you can leave them behind and live right.
verses.kjv: Who his own self bare our sins in his own body on the tree, that we, being dead to sins, should live unto righteousness: by whose stripes ye were healed.

verses.text: Draw near to God, and he will draw near to you. Cleanse your hands, you sinners. Purify your hearts, you double-minded.
verses.meaning: Come close to God and he comes close to you. A double mind needs a single focus: him.
verses.kjv: Draw nigh to God, and he will draw nigh to you. Cleanse your hands, ye sinners; and purify your hearts, ye double minded.

verses.text: Whoever believes that Jesus is the Christ has been born of God. Whoever loves the Father also loves the child who is born of him.
verses.meaning: Trusting that Jesus is the Christ means you’re born into God’s family, so love his other children too.
verses.kjv: Whosoever believeth that Jesus is the Christ is born of God: and every one that loveth him that begat loveth him also that is begotten of him.

verses.text: Finally, all of you be like-minded, compassionate, loving as brothers, tenderhearted, courteous…
verses.meaning: Be people of one heart: caring, kind, humble and quick to feel what others are feeling.
verses.kjv: Finally, be ye all of one mind, having compassion one of another, love as brethren, be pitiful, be courteous…

verses.text: To speak evil of no one, not to be contentious, to be gentle, showing all humility toward all men.
verses.meaning: Peace shows up in how you talk: no trash talk, no picking fights, just gentleness toward everyone.
verses.kjv: To speak evil of no man, to be no brawlers, but gentle, shewing all meekness unto all men.

verses.text: This is love, that we should walk according to his commandments. This is the commandment, even as you heard from the beginning, that you should walk in it.
verses.meaning: God’s kind of love has a shape: walking in his ways, just as you were taught from the start.
verses.kjv: And this is love, that we walk after his commandments. This is the commandment, That, as ye have heard from the beginning, ye should walk in it.

verses.text: Therefore let’s also, seeing we are surrounded by so great a cloud of witnesses, lay aside every weight and the sin which so easily entangles us, and let’s run with perseverance the race that is set before us…
verses.meaning: Faithful people have run before you. Drop what slows you down and keep running the race laid out for you.
verses.kjv: Wherefore seeing we also are compassed about with so great a cloud of witnesses, let us lay aside every weight, and the sin which doth so easily beset us, and let us run with patience the race that is set before us…

verses.text: Not rendering evil for evil or insult for insult; but instead blessing, knowing that you were called to this, that you may inherit a blessing.
verses.meaning: If someone insults you, don’t trade insults back. Answer with a blessing; that’s what you’re called to.
verses.kjv: Not rendering evil for evil, or railing for railing: but contrariwise blessing; knowing that ye are thereunto called, that ye should inherit a blessing.

verses.text: Therefore prepare your minds for action. Be sober, and set your hope fully on the grace that will be brought to you at the revelation of Jesus Christ—
verses.meaning: Get your mind ready, stay clear-headed and put your hope fully on the grace Jesus will bring.
verses.kjv: Wherefore gird up the loins of your mind, be sober, and hope to the end for the grace that is to be brought unto you at the revelation of Jesus Christ…

verses.text: Jude, a servant of Jesus Christ, and brother of James, to those who are called, sanctified by God the Father, and kept for Jesus Christ…
verses.meaning: Jude’s opening words describe you too: called by God, set apart by the Father and kept safe for Jesus.
verses.kjv: Jude, the servant of Jesus Christ, and brother of James, to them that are sanctified by God the Father, and preserved in Jesus Christ, and called…

verses.text: But whoever has the world’s goods and sees his brother in need, then closes his heart of compassion against him, how does God’s love remain in him?
verses.meaning: If you see someone in need and you can help, love doesn’t look away. It opens your heart and hands.
verses.kjv: But whoso hath this world’s good, and seeth his brother have need, and shutteth up his bowels of compassion from him, how dwelleth the love of God in him?

verses.text: The law of truth was in his mouth, and unrighteousness was not found in his lips. He walked with me in peace and uprightness, and turned many away from iniquity.
verses.meaning: God remembered a faithful priest: honest words, a peaceful walk with God, and many helped back to good.
verses.kjv: The law of truth was in his mouth, and iniquity was not found in his lips: he walked with me in peace and equity, and did turn many away from iniquity.

verses.text: As many as I love, I reprove and chasten. Be zealous therefore, and repent.
verses.meaning: When Jesus corrects you, it’s a sign of his love. Take it as an invitation to come back wholeheartedly.
verses.kjv: As many as I love, I rebuke and chasten: be zealous therefore, and repent.

verses.text: But be doers of the word, and not only hearers, deluding your own selves.
verses.meaning: Hearing God’s word without doing it is fooling yourself. Let what you read change what you do today.
verses.kjv: But be ye doers of the word, and not hearers only, deceiving your own selves.

verses.text: The Lord is not slow concerning his promise, as some count slowness; but he is patient with us, not wishing that anyone should perish, but that all should come to repentance.
verses.meaning: God’s patience isn’t slowness. He’s giving everyone room to turn back, because he wants no one lost.
verses.kjv: The Lord is not slack concerning his promise, as some men count slackness; but is longsuffering to us-ward, not willing that any should perish, but that all should come to repentance.

verses.text: Beloved, I beg you as foreigners and pilgrims to abstain from fleshly lusts which war against the soul…
verses.meaning: You’re just passing through this world. Say no to cravings that quietly wage war on your soul.
verses.kjv: Dearly beloved, I beseech you as strangers and pilgrims, abstain from fleshly lusts, which war against the soul…

verses.text: And he made us to be a Kingdom, priests to his God and Father—to him be the glory and the dominion forever and ever. Amen.
verses.meaning: Jesus made you part of his kingdom, and a priest who serves his God and Father.
verses.kjv: And hath made us kings and priests unto God and his Father; to him be glory and dominion for ever and ever. Amen.

verses.text: I have no greater joy than this: to hear about my children walking in truth.
verses.meaning: Nothing brings more joy than seeing the people you’ve poured into keep walking with God.
verses.kjv: I have no greater joy than to hear that my children walk in truth.

verses.text: The world is passing away with its lusts, but he who does God’s will remains forever.
verses.meaning: Trends and cravings fade fast. A life spent doing what God wants is the one that lasts forever.
verses.kjv: And the world passeth away, and the lust thereof: but he that doeth the will of God abideth for ever.

verses.text: But if we walk in the light as he is in the light, we have fellowship with one another, and the blood of Jesus Christ his Son cleanses us from all sin.
verses.meaning: Walking honestly with God keeps you close to others, and Jesus keeps washing you clean of every sin.
verses.kjv: But if we walk in the light, as he is in the light, we have fellowship one with another, and the blood of Jesus Christ his Son cleanseth us from all sin.

verses.text: But the end of all things is near. Therefore be of sound mind, self-controlled, and sober in prayer.
verses.meaning: Because time is short, stay clear-minded and self-controlled. It makes your prayers sharper.
verses.kjv: But the end of all things is at hand: be ye therefore sober, and watch unto prayer.

verses.text: He who has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the assemblies. To him who overcomes, to him I will give of the hidden manna, and I will give him a white stone, and on the stone a new name written which no one knows but he who receives it.
verses.meaning: Jesus promises those who hold on a new name only they will know. Your truest identity is his to give.
verses.kjv: He that hath an ear, let him hear what the Spirit saith unto the churches; To him that overcometh will I give to eat of the hidden manna, and will give him a white stone, and in the stone a new name written, which no man knoweth saving he that receiveth it.

verses.text: But I hope to see you soon. Then we will speak face to face. Peace be to you. The friends greet you. Greet the friends by name.
verses.meaning: Letters were good, but John wanted to talk face to face. Know your friends and greet them by name.
verses.kjv: But I trust I shall shortly see thee, and we shall speak face to face. Peace be to thee. Our friends salute thee. Greet the friends by name.

verses.text: My little children, I write these things to you so that you may not sin. If anyone sins, we have a Counselor with the Father, Jesus Christ, the righteous. And he is the atoning sacrifice for our sins, and not for ours only, but also for the whole world.
verses.meaning: If you mess up, you’re not on your own: Jesus speaks up for you and has already paid for your sin.
verses.kjv: My little children, these things write I unto you, that ye sin not. And if any man sin, we have an advocate with the Father, Jesus Christ the righteous: And he is the propitiation for our sins: and not for ours only, but also for the sins of the whole world.

verses.text: For all that is in the world—the lust of the flesh, the lust of the eyes, and the pride of life—isn’t the Father’s, but is the world’s.
verses.meaning: Craving, wanting what you see and showing off don’t come from the Father. Notice what’s pulling at you.
verses.kjv: For all that is in the world, the lust of the flesh, and the lust of the eyes, and the pride of life, is not of the Father, but is of the world.

verses.text: After these things I looked, and behold, a great multitude which no man could count, out of every nation and of all tribes, peoples, and languages, standing before the throne and before the Lamb, dressed in white robes, with palm branches in their hands.
verses.meaning: Heaven will be crowded with people from every nation and language, worshiping together as one family.
verses.kjv: After this I beheld, and, lo, a great multitude, which no man could number, of all nations, and kindreds, and people, and tongues, stood before the throne, and before the Lamb, clothed with white robes, and palms in their hands…

verses.text: If then you count me a partner, receive him as you would receive me. But if he has wronged you at all or owes you anything, put that to my account.
verses.meaning: Paul asked a friend to welcome back a runaway as family and to charge any debt to Paul’s own account.
verses.kjv: If thou count me therefore a partner, receive him as myself. If he hath wronged thee, or oweth thee ought, put that on mine account…

verses.text: Little children, keep yourselves from idols.
verses.meaning: John ends his letter with a short warning: guard your heart from anything that takes God’s place.
verses.kjv: Little children, keep yourselves from idols. Amen.

verses.text: But I have this against you, that you left your first love.
verses.meaning: A church busy doing right had lost its first love. Make sure Jesus has your heart, not just your effort.
verses.kjv: Nevertheless I have somewhat against thee, because thou hast left thy first love.

facts.text: Methuselah is the oldest person in the Bible: he lived 969 years.
facts.verseText: All the days of Methuselah were nine hundred sixty-nine years, then he died.

facts.text: “Jesus wept.” is the shortest verse in the Bible, found in John 11:35.
facts.verseText: Jesus wept.

facts.text: Psalm 117 is the shortest chapter in the Bible, just two verses long.
facts.verseText: Praise the LORD, all you nations! Extol him, all you peoples! For his loving kindness is great toward us. The LORD’s faithfulness endures forever. Praise the LORD!

facts.text: Psalm 119 is the longest chapter in the Bible, with 176 verses.
facts.verseText: I have gone astray like a lost sheep. Seek your servant, for I don’t forget your commandments.

facts.text: The refrain “for his loving kindness endures forever” ends all 26 verses of Psalm 136.
facts.verseText: Give thanks to the LORD, for he is good, for his loving kindness endures forever. Give thanks to the God of gods, for his loving kindness endures forever. Give thanks to the Lord of lords, for his loving kindness endures forever; to him who alone does great wonders, for his loving kindness endures forever; to him who by understanding made the heavens, for his loving kindness endures forever; to him who spread out the earth above the waters, for his loving kindness endures forever; to him who made the great lights, for his loving kindness endures forever; the sun to rule by day, for his loving kindness endures forever; the moon and stars to rule by night, for his loving kindness endures forever; to him who struck down the Egyptian firstborn, for his loving kindness endures forever; and brought out Israel from among them, for his loving kindness endures forever; with a strong hand, and with an outstretched arm, for his loving kindness endures forever; to him who divided the Red Sea apart, for his loving kindness endures forever; and made Israel to pass through the middle of it, for his loving kindness endures forever; but overthrew Pharaoh and his army in the Red Sea, for his loving kindness endures forever; to him who led his people through the wilderness, for his loving kindness endures forever; to him who struck great kings, for his loving kindness endures forever; and killed mighty kings, for his loving kindness endures forever; Sihon king of the Amorites, for his loving kindness endures forever; Og king of Bashan, for his loving kindness endures forever; and gave their land as an inheritance, for his loving kindness endures forever; even a heritage to Israel his servant, for his loving kindness endures forever; who remembered us in our low estate, for his loving kindness endures forever; and has delivered us from our adversaries, for his loving kindness endures forever; who gives food to every creature, for his loving kindness endures forever. Oh give thanks to the God of heaven, for his loving kindness endures forever.

facts.text: The longest verse in the Bible is Esther 8:9, a royal decree sent to 127 provinces from India to Ethiopia.
facts.verseText: Then the king’s scribes were called at that time, in the third month, which is the month Sivan, on the twenty-third day of the month; and it was written according to all that Mordecai commanded to the Jews, and to the local governors, and the governors and princes of the provinces which are from India to Ethiopia, one hundred twenty-seven provinces, to every province according to its writing, and to every people in their language, and to the Jews in their writing, and in their language.

facts.text: The Bible’s very last word is “Amen,” closing a blessing of grace on all the saints.
facts.verseText: The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ be with all the saints. Amen.

facts.text: Obadiah has the fewest verses of any Old Testament book: one chapter of just 21 verses.
facts.verseText: Saviors will go up on Mount Zion to judge the mountains of Esau, and the kingdom will be the LORD’s.

facts.text: Second John has only 13 verses, the fewest of any book in the Bible.
facts.verseText: The children of your chosen sister greet you. Amen.

facts.text: King Og of Bashan had an iron bed nine cubits long and four cubits wide.
facts.verseText: (For only Og king of Bashan remained of the remnant of the Rephaim. Behold, his bedstead was a bedstead of iron. Isn’t it in Rabbah of the children of Ammon? Nine cubits was its length, and four cubits its width, after the cubit of a man.)

facts.text: A giant at Gath had six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot: 24 in all.
facts.verseText: There was again war at Gath, where there was a man of great stature, who had six fingers on every hand and six toes on every foot, twenty-four in number, and he also was born to the giant.

facts.text: Balaam’s donkey spoke to him, asking why he had struck her three times.
facts.verseText: The LORD opened the mouth of the donkey, and she said to Balaam, “What have I done to you, that you have struck me these three times?”

facts.text: The tribe of Benjamin had 700 chosen left-handed men who could sling a stone at a hair and not miss.
facts.verseText: The children of Benjamin were counted on that day out of the cities twenty-six thousand men who drew the sword, in addition to the inhabitants of Gibeah, who were counted seven hundred chosen men. Among all these soldiers there were seven hundred chosen men who were left-handed. Every one of them could sling a stone at a hair and not miss.

facts.text: Eutychus fell asleep during Paul’s long talk and fell from a third floor window, but he was brought back alive.
facts.verseText: A certain young man named Eutychus sat in the window, weighed down with deep sleep. As Paul spoke still longer, being weighed down by his sleep, he fell down from the third floor and was taken up dead. Paul went down and fell upon him, and embracing him said, “Don’t be troubled, for his life is in him.” When he had gone up, had broken bread and eaten, and had talked with them a long while, even until break of day, he departed. They brought the boy in alive, and were greatly comforted.

facts.text: The Bible says Enoch walked with God and then simply was not found, because God took him.
facts.verseText: Enoch walked with God, and he was not found, for God took him.

facts.text: Samson struck down a thousand men with the fresh jawbone of a donkey.
facts.verseText: He found a fresh jawbone of a donkey, put out his hand, took it, and struck a thousand men with it.

facts.text: King Solomon spoke 3,000 proverbs, and his songs numbered 1,005.
facts.verseText: He spoke three thousand proverbs, and his songs numbered one thousand five.

facts.text: Ravens brought Elijah bread and meat every morning and every evening.
facts.verseText: The ravens brought him bread and meat in the morning, and bread and meat in the evening; and he drank from the brook.

facts.text: People laid the sick in the streets, hoping Peter’s shadow would fall on them as he passed.
facts.verseText: They even carried out the sick into the streets and laid them on cots and mattresses, so that as Peter came by, at least his shadow might overshadow some of them.

facts.text: Zacchaeus was too short to see Jesus over the crowd, so he climbed a sycamore tree.
facts.verseText: He was trying to see who Jesus was, and couldn’t because of the crowd, because he was short. He ran on ahead and climbed up into a sycamore tree to see him, for he was going to pass that way.

facts.text: Jesus’ first sign was turning water into wine at a wedding in Cana.
facts.verseText: The third day, there was a wedding in Cana of Galilee. Jesus’ mother was there. Jesus also was invited, with his disciples, to the wedding. When the wine ran out, Jesus’ mother said to him, “They have no wine.” Jesus said to her, “Woman, what does that have to do with you and me? My hour has not yet come.” His mother said to the servants, “Whatever he says to you, do it.” Now there were six water pots of stone set there after the Jews’ way of purifying, containing two or three metretes apiece. Jesus said to them, “Fill the water pots with water.” So they filled them up to the brim. He said to them, “Now draw some out, and take it to the ruler of the feast.” So they took it. When the ruler of the feast tasted the water now become wine, and didn’t know where it came from (but the servants who had drawn the water knew), the ruler of the feast called the bridegroom and said to him, “Everyone serves the good wine first, and when the guests have drunk freely, then that which is worse. You have kept the good wine until now!” This beginning of his signs Jesus did in Cana of Galilee, and revealed his glory; and his disciples believed in him.

facts.text: Followers of Jesus were first called “Christians” in the city of Antioch.
facts.verseText: When he had found him, he brought him to Antioch. For a whole year they were gathered together with the assembly, and taught many people. The disciples were first called Christians in Antioch.

facts.text: After the resurrection, Peter hauled in a net holding 153 large fish, and it didn’t tear.
facts.verseText: Simon Peter went up, and drew the net to land, full of one hundred fifty-three great fish. Even though there were so many, the net wasn’t torn.

facts.text: The prophet Elisha once made a borrowed iron ax head float on the water.
facts.verseText: But as one was cutting down a tree, the ax head fell into the water. Then he cried out and said, “Alas, my master! For it was borrowed.” The man of God asked, “Where did it fall?” He showed him the place. He cut down a stick, threw it in there, and made the iron float.

facts.text: Moses’ face shone after he spoke with God, and he didn’t even know it.
facts.verseText: When Moses came down from Mount Sinai with the two tablets of the covenant in Moses’ hand, when he came down from the mountain, Moses didn’t know that the skin of his face shone by reason of his speaking with him.

facts.text: Moses was 120 years old when he died, and his eyesight and strength were still strong.
facts.verseText: Moses was one hundred twenty years old when he died. His eye was not dim, nor his strength gone.

facts.text: Manna was white like coriander seed and tasted like wafers made with honey.
facts.verseText: The house of Israel called its name “Manna”, and it was like coriander seed, white; and its taste was like wafers with honey.

facts.text: Jacob worked seven years to marry Rachel, and it felt like a few days because he loved her.
facts.verseText: Jacob served seven years for Rachel. They seemed to him but a few days, for the love he had for her.

facts.text: When the twins Esau and Jacob were born, Jacob came out holding on to Esau’s heel.
facts.verseText: The first came out red all over, like a hairy garment. They named him Esau. After that, his brother came out, and his hand had hold on Esau’s heel. He was named Jacob. Isaac was sixty years old when she bore them.

facts.text: King Nebuchadnezzar was driven away from people and ate grass like an ox.
facts.verseText: This was fulfilled the same hour on Nebuchadnezzar. He was driven from men and ate grass like oxen; and his body was wet with the dew of the sky until his hair had grown like eagles’ feathers, and his nails like birds’ claws.

facts.text: Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego walked out of the fiery furnace without even the smell of fire on them.
facts.verseText: Then Nebuchadnezzar came near to the mouth of the burning fiery furnace. He spoke and said, “Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, you servants of the Most High God, come out, and come here!” Then Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego came out of the middle of the fire. The local governors, the deputies, and the governors, and the king’s counselors, being gathered together, saw these men, that the fire had no power on their bodies. The hair of their head wasn’t singed. Their pants weren’t changed. The smell of fire wasn’t even on them.

facts.text: Absalom cut his hair once a year because it grew so heavy, and it weighed 200 shekels.
facts.verseText: Now in all Israel there was no one to be so much praised as Absalom for his beauty. From the sole of his foot even to the crown of his head there was no defect in him. When he cut the hair of his head (now it was at every year’s end that he cut it; because it was heavy on him, therefore he cut it), he weighed the hair of his head at two hundred shekels, after the king’s weight.

facts.text: When Peter knocked at the gate, Rhoda was so overjoyed that she ran inside without opening it.
facts.verseText: When Peter knocked at the door of the gate, a servant girl named Rhoda came to answer. When she recognized Peter’s voice, she didn’t open the gate for joy, but ran in and reported that Peter was standing in front of the gate.

facts.text: A viper fastened onto Paul’s hand, but he shook it off into the fire and wasn’t harmed.
facts.verseText: But when Paul had gathered a bundle of sticks and laid them on the fire, a viper came out because of the heat and fastened on his hand. When the natives saw the creature hanging from his hand, they said to one another, “No doubt this man is a murderer, whom, though he has escaped from the sea, yet Justice has not allowed to live.” However he shook off the creature into the fire, and wasn’t harmed.

facts.text: Overnight, Aaron’s staff sprouted, budded, blossomed and grew ripe almonds.
facts.verseText: On the next day, Moses went into the Tent of the Testimony; and behold, Aaron’s rod for the house of Levi had sprouted, budded, produced blossoms, and bore ripe almonds.

facts.text: A dead man came back to life when his body touched the bones of the prophet Elisha.
facts.verseText: As they were burying a man, behold, they saw a band of raiders; and they threw the man into Elisha’s tomb. As soon as the man touched Elisha’s bones, he revived, and stood up on his feet.

facts.text: During a fierce storm at sea, Jesus was asleep in the back of the boat on a cushion.
facts.verseText: A big wind storm arose, and the waves beat into the boat, so much that the boat was already filled. He himself was in the stern, asleep on the cushion; and they woke him up and asked him, “Teacher, don’t you care that we are dying?”

facts.text: The risen Jesus met his disciples at a coal fire with fish and bread and invited them to come and eat breakfast.
facts.verseText: So when they got out on the land, they saw a fire of coals there, with fish and bread laid on it. Jesus said to them, “Bring some of the fish which you have just caught.” Simon Peter went up, and drew the net to land, full of one hundred fifty-three great fish. Even though there were so many, the net wasn’t torn. Jesus said to them, “Come and eat breakfast!” None of the disciples dared inquire of him, “Who are you?” knowing that it was the Lord.

facts.text: When Mary Magdalene first saw the risen Jesus, she thought he was the gardener.
facts.verseText: Jesus said to her, “Woman, why are you weeping? Who are you looking for?” She, supposing him to be the gardener, said to him, “Sir, if you have carried him away, tell me where you have laid him, and I will take him away.”

facts.text: Israel’s scouts carried back a single cluster of grapes on a staff between two men.
facts.verseText: They came to the valley of Eshcol, and cut down from there a branch with one cluster of grapes, and they bore it on a staff between two. They also brought some of the pomegranates and figs.

facts.text: Ruth was King David’s great-grandmother: her son Obed was the father of Jesse, David’s father.
facts.verseText: So Boaz took Ruth and she became his wife; and he went in to her, and the LORD enabled her to conceive, and she bore a son. The women said to Naomi, “Blessed be the LORD, who has not left you today without a near kinsman. Let his name be famous in Israel. He shall be to you a restorer of life and sustain you in your old age; for your daughter-in-law, who loves you, who is better to you than seven sons, has given birth to him.” Naomi took the child, laid him in her bosom, and became nurse to him. The women, her neighbors, gave him a name, saying, “A son is born to Naomi”. They named him Obed. He is the father of Jesse, the father of David.

facts.text: A woman named Rahab appears in Jesus’ family tree as the mother of Boaz.
facts.verseText: Salmon became the father of Boaz by Rahab. Boaz became the father of Obed by Ruth. Obed became the father of Jesse.

facts.text: At 85, Caleb said he was just as strong as on the day Moses first sent him out.
facts.verseText: Now, behold, the LORD has kept me alive, as he spoke, these forty-five years, from the time that the LORD spoke this word to Moses, while Israel walked in the wilderness. Now, behold, I am eighty-five years old, today. As yet I am as strong today as I was in the day that Moses sent me. As my strength was then, even so is my strength now for war, to go out and to come in.

facts.text: God blessed the end of Job’s life more than the beginning: 14,000 sheep and 6,000 camels.
facts.verseText: So the LORD blessed the latter end of Job more than his beginning. He had fourteen thousand sheep, six thousand camels, one thousand yoke of oxen, and a thousand female donkeys.

facts.text: Under Nehemiah, the wall of Jerusalem was rebuilt in just 52 days.
facts.verseText: So the wall was finished in the twenty-fifth day of Elul, in fifty-two days.

facts.text: Noah knew the flood waters were going down when a dove came back with a fresh olive leaf.
facts.verseText: The dove came back to him at evening and, behold, in her mouth was a freshly plucked olive leaf. So Noah knew that the waters were abated from the earth.

facts.text: Every three years, King Solomon’s fleet came home with gold, silver, ivory, apes and peacocks.
facts.verseText: For the king had a fleet of ships of Tarshish at sea with Hiram’s fleet. Once every three years the fleet of Tarshish came bringing gold, silver, ivory, apes, and peacocks.

facts.text: John the Baptizer wore clothing of camel’s hair and ate locusts and wild honey.
facts.verseText: Now John himself wore clothing made of camel’s hair with a leather belt around his waist. His food was locusts and wild honey.

facts.text: At midnight in prison, Paul and Silas prayed and sang hymns while the other prisoners listened.
facts.verseText: But about midnight Paul and Silas were praying and singing hymns to God, and the prisoners were listening to them.

facts.text: Saul, later called Paul, escaped Damascus at night when friends lowered him through the wall in a basket.
facts.verseText: But Saul increased more in strength, and confounded the Jews who lived at Damascus, proving that this is the Christ. When many days were fulfilled, the Jews conspired together to kill him, but their plot became known to Saul. They watched the gates both day and night that they might kill him, but his disciples took him by night and let him down through the wall, lowering him in a basket.

facts.text: Queen Esther was also called Hadassah, and her cousin Mordecai raised her as his own daughter.
facts.verseText: He brought up Hadassah, that is, Esther, his uncle’s daughter; for she had neither father nor mother. The maiden was fair and beautiful; and when her father and mother were dead, Mordecai took her for his own daughter.

facts.text: Barnabas, which means “Son of Encouragement,” was the nickname the apostles gave to a Levite named Joses.
facts.verseText: Joses, who by the apostles was also called Barnabas (which is, being interpreted, Son of Encouragement), a Levite, a man of Cyprus by race…

facts.text: “Sons of Thunder” is what Jesus called the brothers James and John, giving them the name Boanerges.
facts.verseText: James the son of Zebedee; and John, the brother of James, (whom he called Boanerges, which means, Sons of Thunder)…

facts.text: With the words “Talitha cumi,” meaning “Girl, I tell you, get up,” Jesus raised a twelve-year-old girl.
facts.verseText: Taking the child by the hand, he said to her, “Talitha cumi!” which means, being interpreted, “Girl, I tell you, get up!” Immediately the girl rose up and walked, for she was twelve years old. They were amazed with great amazement.

facts.text: Pharaoh’s daughter named the baby Moses because she drew him out of the water.
facts.verseText: The child grew, and she brought him to Pharaoh’s daughter, and he became her son. She named him Moses, and said, “Because I drew him out of the water.”

facts.text: According to the book of Job, God “hangs the earth on nothing” and stretches the north over empty space.
facts.verseText: He stretches out the north over empty space, and hangs the earth on nothing.

facts.text: The wise men found the young Jesus in a house and gave him gold, frankincense and myrrh.
facts.verseText: They came into the house and saw the young child with Mary, his mother, and they fell down and worshiped him. Opening their treasures, they offered to him gifts: gold, frankincense, and myrrh.

facts.text: The LORD wasn’t in the wind, the earthquake or the fire. After them came a still small voice.
facts.verseText: He said, “Go out and stand on the mountain before the LORD.” Behold, the LORD passed by, and a great and strong wind tore the mountains and broke in pieces the rocks before the LORD; but the LORD was not in the wind. After the wind there was an earthquake; but the LORD was not in the earthquake. After the earthquake a fire passed; but the LORD was not in the fire. After the fire, there was a still small voice.

facts.text: Jesus told Peter he would find a coin in a fish’s mouth to pay the tax for them both.
facts.verseText: When they had come to Capernaum, those who collected the didrachma coins came to Peter, and said, “Doesn’t your teacher pay the didrachma?” He said, “Yes.” When he came into the house, Jesus anticipated him, saying, “What do you think, Simon? From whom do the kings of the earth receive toll or tribute? From their children, or from strangers?” Peter said to him, “From strangers.” Jesus said to him, “Therefore the children are exempt. But, lest we cause them to stumble, go to the sea, cast a hook, and take up the first fish that comes up. When you have opened its mouth, you will find a stater coin. Take that, and give it to them for me and you.”

facts.text: Timothy’s faith lived first in his grandmother Lois and his mother Eunice.
facts.verseText: Having been reminded of the sincere faith that is in you, which lived first in your grandmother Lois and your mother Eunice and, I am persuaded, in you also.

whoSaid.quote: Where you go, I will go; and where you stay, I will stay. Your people will be my people, and your God my God.
whoSaid.speaker: Ruth

whoSaid.quote: Sun, stand still on Gibeon! You, moon, stop in the valley of Aijalon!
whoSaid.speaker: Joshua

whoSaid.quote: Then I will go in to the king, which is against the law; and if I perish, I perish.
whoSaid.speaker: Esther

whoSaid.quote: Who knows if you haven’t come to the kingdom for such a time as this?
whoSaid.speaker: Mordecai

whoSaid.quote: I don’t know. Am I my brother’s keeper?
whoSaid.speaker: Cain

whoSaid.quote: God will provide himself the lamb for a burnt offering, my son.
whoSaid.speaker: Abraham

whoSaid.quote: You meant evil against me, but God meant it for good
whoSaid.speaker: Joseph

whoSaid.quote: Who is the LORD, that I should listen to his voice to let Israel go?
whoSaid.speaker: Pharaoh

whoSaid.quote: I threw it into the fire, and out came this calf.
whoSaid.speaker: Aaron

whoSaid.quote: Let’s go up at once, and possess it; for we are well able to overcome it!
whoSaid.speaker: Caleb

whoSaid.quote: What have I done to you, that you have struck me these three times?
whoSaid.speaker: Balaam’s donkey

whoSaid.quote: If you will go with me, then I will go; but if you will not go with me, I will not go.
whoSaid.speaker: Barak

whoSaid.quote: Remember me, please, and strengthen me, please, only this once, God
whoSaid.speaker: Samson

whoSaid.quote: All the city of my people knows that you are a worthy woman
whoSaid.speaker: Boaz

whoSaid.quote: I am a woman of a sorrowful spirit.
whoSaid.speaker: Hannah

whoSaid.quote: Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice, and to listen than the fat of rams.
whoSaid.speaker: Samuel

whoSaid.quote: You come to me with a sword, with a spear, and with a javelin; but I come to you in the name of the LORD of Armies
whoSaid.speaker: David

whoSaid.quote: You are the man! This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says
whoSaid.speaker: Nathan

whoSaid.quote: Behold, not even half was told me! Your wisdom and prosperity exceed the fame which I heard.
whoSaid.speaker: Queen of Sheba

whoSaid.quote: My father made your yoke heavy, but I will add to your yoke.
whoSaid.speaker: Rehoboam

whoSaid.quote: How long will you waver between the two sides? If the LORD is God, follow him
whoSaid.speaker: Elijah

whoSaid.quote: Please let a double portion of your spirit be on me.
whoSaid.speaker: Elisha

whoSaid.quote: Naked I came out of my mother’s womb, and naked will I return there.
whoSaid.speaker: Job

whoSaid.quote: My God has sent his angel, and has shut the lions’ mouths, and they have not hurt me
whoSaid.speaker: Daniel

whoSaid.quote: See now, I know that there is no God in all the earth, but in Israel.
whoSaid.speaker: Naaman

whoSaid.quote: Give me children, or else I will die.
whoSaid.speaker: Rachel

whoSaid.quote: For man looks at the outward appearance, but the LORD looks at the heart.
whoSaid.speaker: God

whoSaid.quote: Where were you when I laid the foundations of the earth?
whoSaid.speaker: God

whoSaid.quote: Shouldn’t I be concerned for Nineveh, that great city
whoSaid.speaker: God

whoSaid.quote: You are the Christ, the Son of the living God.
whoSaid.speaker: Peter

whoSaid.quote: Unless I see in his hands the print of the nails, put my finger into the print of the nails, and put my hand into his side, I will not believe.
whoSaid.speaker: Thomas

whoSaid.quote: Can any good thing come out of Nazareth?
whoSaid.speaker: Nathanael

whoSaid.quote: How can a man be born when he is old?
whoSaid.speaker: Nicodemus

whoSaid.quote: Lord, don’t you care that my sister left me to serve alone?
whoSaid.speaker: Martha

whoSaid.quote: Behold, the servant of the Lord; let it be done to me according to your word.
whoSaid.speaker: Mary

whoSaid.quote: How can I be sure of this? For I am an old man, and my wife is well advanced in years.
whoSaid.speaker: Zacharias

whoSaid.quote: Blessed are you among women, and blessed is the fruit of your womb!
whoSaid.speaker: Elizabeth

whoSaid.quote: Now you are releasing your servant, Master, according to your word, in peace
whoSaid.speaker: Simeon

whoSaid.quote: Behold, Lord, half of my goods I give to the poor.
whoSaid.speaker: Zacchaeus

whoSaid.quote: What I have written, I have written.
whoSaid.speaker: Pilate

whoSaid.quote: It is advantageous for us that one man should die for the people
whoSaid.speaker: Caiaphas

whoSaid.quote: This is John the Baptizer. He is risen from the dead.
whoSaid.speaker: Herod

whoSaid.quote: I have no silver or gold, but what I have, that I give you.
whoSaid.speaker: Peter

whoSaid.quote: With a little persuasion are you trying to make me a Christian?
whoSaid.speaker: Agrippa

whoSaid.quote: My little daughter is at the point of death. Please come and lay your hands on her
whoSaid.speaker: Jairus

whoSaid.quote: Jesus, you son of David, have mercy on me!
whoSaid.speaker: Bartimaeus

whoSaid.quote: You will never wash my feet!
whoSaid.speaker: Peter

whoSaid.quote: Lord, show us the Father, and that will be enough for us.
whoSaid.speaker: Philip

whoSaid.quote: There is a boy here who has five barley loaves and two fish
whoSaid.speaker: Andrew

whoSaid.quote: Why wasn’t this ointment sold for three hundred denarii and given to the poor?
whoSaid.speaker: Judas

whoSaid.quote: Lord, I have heard from many about this man, how much evil he did to your saints at Jerusalem.
whoSaid.speaker: Ananias

whoSaid.quote: If this counsel or this work is of men, it will be overthrown.
whoSaid.speaker: Gamaliel

whoSaid.quote: If you have judged me to be faithful to the Lord, come into my house and stay.
whoSaid.speaker: Lydia

whoSaid.quote: I also found an altar with this inscription: ‘TO AN UNKNOWN GOD.’
whoSaid.speaker: Paul

whoSaid.quote: I am the resurrection and the life.
whoSaid.speaker: Jesus

whoSaid.quote: Cheer up! It is I! Don’t be afraid.
whoSaid.speaker: Jesus

whoSaid.quote: Martha, Martha, you are anxious and troubled about many things
whoSaid.speaker: Jesus

whoSaid.quote: Simon, son of Jonah, do you love me more than these?
whoSaid.speaker: Jesus

whoSaid.quote: Get behind me, Satan! You are a stumbling block to me
whoSaid.speaker: Jesus

whoSaid.quote: You shall tell the children of Israel this: ‘I AM has sent me to you.’
whoSaid.speaker: God

finish.text: For God so loved the world, that he gave his only born Son, that whoever believes in him should not perish, but have eternal life.
I can do all things through Christ who strengthens me.
A Psalm by David. The LORD is my shepherd; I shall lack nothing.
“For I know the thoughts that I think toward you,” says the LORD, “thoughts of peace, and not of evil, to give you hope and a future.”
Trust in the LORD with all your heart, and don’t lean on your own understanding. In all your ways acknowledge him, and he will make your paths straight.
We know that all things work together for good for those who love God, for those who are called according to his purpose.
But those who wait for the LORD will renew their strength. They will mount up with wings like eagles. They will run, and not be weary. They will walk, and not faint.
Come to me, all you who labor and are heavily burdened, and I will give you rest.
Jesus said to him, “I am the way, the truth, and the life. No one comes to the Father, except through me.”
Your word is a lamp to my feet, and a light for my path.
Now faith is assurance of things hoped for, proof of things not seen.
For God didn’t give us a spirit of fear, but of power, love, and self-control.
He who doesn’t love doesn’t know God, for God is love.
But seek first God’s Kingdom and his righteousness; and all these things will be given to you as well.
This is the day that the LORD has made. We will rejoice and be glad in it!
The LORD’s name is a strong tower: the righteous run to him, and are safe.
Blessed are the peacemakers, for they shall be called children of God.
Blessed are the pure in heart, for they shall see God.
You are the light of the world. A city located on a hill can’t be hidden.
You will know the truth, and the truth will make you free.
But now faith, hope, and love remain—these three. The greatest of these is love.
Let all that you do be done in love.
Let’s not be weary in doing good, for we will reap in due season if we don’t give up.
Oh taste and see that the LORD is good. Blessed is the man who takes refuge in him.
Also delight yourself in the LORD, and he will give you the desires of your heart.
Create in me a clean heart, O God. Renew a right spirit within me.
I will give thanks to you, for I am fearfully and wonderfully made. Your works are wonderful. My soul knows that very well.
For nothing spoken by God is impossible.
For the wages of sin is death, but the free gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord.
For all have sinned, and fall short of the glory of God…
And be kind to one another, tender hearted, forgiving each other, just as God also in Christ forgave you.
Casting all your worries on him, because he cares for you.
Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever.
For the Chief Musician. By the sons of Korah. According to Alamoth. God is our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble.
A Song of Ascents. I will lift up my eyes to the hills. Where does my help come from? My help comes from the LORD, who made heaven and earth.
Commit your deeds to the LORD, and your plans shall succeed.
A man’s heart plans his course, but the LORD directs his steps.
A friend loves at all times; and a brother is born for adversity.
Iron sharpens iron; so a man sharpens his friend’s countenance.
A gentle answer turns away wrath, but a harsh word stirs up anger.
For everything there is a season, and a time for every purpose under heaven…
If a man prevails against one who is alone, two shall withstand him; and a threefold cord is not quickly broken.
‘The LORD bless you, and keep you. The LORD make his face to shine on you, and be gracious to you. The LORD lift up his face toward you, and give you peace.’
Looking at them, Jesus said, “With men this is impossible, but with God all things are possible.”
When I am afraid, I will put my trust in you.
You will keep whoever’s mind is steadfast in perfect peace, because he trusts in you.
I am the vine. You are the branches. He who remains in me and I in him bears much fruit, for apart from me you can do nothing.
Therefore if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation. The old things have passed away. Behold, all things have become new.
But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faith, gentleness, and self-control. Against such things there is no law.
For the Chief Musician. A Psalm by David. The heavens declare the glory of God. The expanse shows his handiwork.
Let the words of my mouth and the meditation of my heart be acceptable in your sight, LORD, my rock, and my redeemer.
For his anger is but for a moment. His favor is for a lifetime. Weeping may stay for the night, but joy comes in the morning.
As far as the east is from the west, so far has he removed our transgressions from us.
The grass withers, the flower fades; but the word of our God stands forever.
As you would like people to do to you, do exactly so to them.
In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.
The light shines in the darkness, and the darkness hasn’t overcome it.
Greater love has no one than this, that someone lay down his life for his friends.
In the beginning, God created the heavens and the earth.
The LORD will fight for you, and you shall be still.
You shall love the LORD your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your might.
He who dwells in the secret place of the Most High will rest in the shadow of the Almighty.
Train up a child in the way he should go, and when he is old he will not depart from it.
A Song of Ascents. By David. See how good and how pleasant it is for brothers to live together in unity!
If we confess our sins, he is faithful and righteous to forgive us the sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.
We love him, because he first loved us.
For where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.
He must increase, but I must decrease.
What then shall we say about these things? If God is for us, who can be against us?
But God commends his own love toward us, in that while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us.
For we walk by faith, not by sight.
The LORD is near to those who have a broken heart, and saves those who have a crushed spirit.
Haven’t I commanded you? Be strong and courageous. Don’t be afraid. Don’t be dismayed, for the LORD your God is with you wherever you go.
Don’t you be afraid, for I am with you. Don’t be dismayed, for I am your God. I will strengthen you. Yes, I will help you. Yes, I will uphold you with the right hand of my righteousness.
He has shown you, O man, what is good. What does the LORD require of you, but to act justly, to love mercy, and to walk humbly with your God?
Even though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil, for you are with me. Your rod and your staff, they comfort me.
I have told you these things, that in me you may have peace. In the world you have trouble; but cheer up! I have overcome the world.
He heals the broken in heart, and binds up their wounds.
